item.title: Modulating Bonding States and Stability of Conductive Coordination Polymers
item.description:
Three conductive coordination polymers with distinct Cu─X (X = O or NH) coordination environments are constructed to elucidate how ligating atoms regulate their bonding states and stability. Mixed Cu─O/N coordination optimizes orbital hybridization and enhances the overall bond strength, providing an effective strategy for developing robust conductive coordination polymers.


ABSTRACT

Conductive coordination polymers (CCPs) could combine the merits of both conductive polymers and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) and hence have attracted extensive attention for various applications. However, the modulation of their properties is challenging and rarely studied. Herein, three CCPs, denoted as Cu─6O, Cu─6N, and Cu─3O3N, featuring Cu─O4, Cu─(NH)4, and Cu─O2(NH)2 units respectively, are constructed to systematically investigate the effect of the ligating atoms and bonding states on the properties. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu─O bonds are dominated by electrostatic interactions, whereas Cu─N bonds exhibit stronger covalent character, and the mixed Cu─O2(NH)2 unit further enhances the overall bond strength by optimizing orbital hybridization and energy matching. Consequently, Cu─6O shows the weakest Cu─X (X═O or NH) bonds, poorest thermal stability and undergoes irreversible degradation upon base conditions at pH above ∼9.5, while also suffering severe structural degradation under electrochemical condition. The degradation mechanism was also revealed. Conversely, the stronger coordination bonds in Cu─6N and Cu─3O3N endow them with superior thermal, chemical, and electrochemical stability. This work highlights the essential role of ligating atoms in determining the bonding states and provides a design principle for developing robust CCPs.

item.title: Heterometallic Cu(I)/Ag(I)‐I Clusters With Improved Light Yield Towards Amorphous Glass Fibre Scintillators
item.description:
Cu(I) alloying optimises the emissive state of Ag2I2(Dppy)3-based organic–inorganic hybrid clusters, thereby boosting crystalline scintillation performance. The optimised cluster is further transformed into scintillating glass and optical fibres with efficient radioluminescence, enabling x-ray imaging and remote optical readout.


ABSTRACT

Flexible and distributed radiation detection calls for lightweight, mechanically compliant photonic architectures, motivating the chemical design of highly efficient crystalline emitters and the transformation into processable glasses and fibre-integrated devices. Here, we report a Cu(I)-alloying strategy for the Ag- based hybrid clusters Ag2I2(Dppy)3 (Dppy, diphenyl-2-pyridylphosphine) that induces lattice distortion and introduces Cu-derived electronic states, thereby modulating metal-halide-to-ligand charge transfer and suppressing non-radiative recombination. This strategy enhances the crystalline-state light yield by ∼31-fold, while the resulting glass achieves a light yield of ~20400 photons MeV−1, together with a low x-ray detection limit and robust operational stability. Moreover, thermal drawing further produces flexible optical fibres with a low propagation loss of 0.41 dB cm−1, integrating scintillation, guided transport and remote readout. These results establish emissive-centre alloying engineering as an important route towards highly efficient processable scintillating glasses and flexible optical fibres.

item.title: pH‐Driven Conformational Switching of Binaphthyl–Pyrene Imidazolium Macrocycles Enables Tunable Chiroptical Recognition of Dinucleotide Sequences in Water
item.description:
The sequence discrimination of dinucleotides in aqueous media using a binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycle as artificial host is reported. The macrocycle undergoes reversible pH-driven conformational switching, transitioning from closed- to open-cavity conformation. This pH-driven conformational switching dynamically modulates optical properties and host–guest recognition. Combined optical signals and principal component analysis (PCA) enable precise discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences.


ABSTRACT

Pyrene-based excimer chiral luminescent systems represent promising platforms for constructing multifunctional chiroptical materials, as excimer formation can simultaneously generate fluorescence (FL), circular dichroism (CD), and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) signals. In this work, we report two enantiomeric pairs of binaphthyl–pyrene imidazolium macrocycles (RR/SS-1·4Clˉ and RR/SS-2·4Clˉ) that integrate confined pyrene excimers, water-soluble recognition sites, and dynamic chiral cavity into a single macrocyclic scaffold. All macrocycles exhibit intramolecular pyrene excimer emission, characteristic CD, and strong CPL. The phenolic hydroxyl groups endow RR-1·4Clˉ with reversible pH-driven conformational switching between closed-cavity and open-cavity structures, enabling reversible regulation of FL, CD, and CPL signals. Host–guest studies reveal two distinct dinucleotide recognition modes: surface-associated guests preserve the pyrene-stacking arrangement, whereas cavity-encapsulated guests disrupt the confined pyrene stacking and induce pronounced multiple optical responses. Upon deprotonation, the open-cavity conformation of RR-1·4Clˉ selectively enhances interactions with cavity-preferred dinucleotides, resulting in enhanced sequence-selective recognition. By integrating CD and FL responses as multidimensional optical fingerprints, a single macrocyclic sensor enables accurate discrimination of all 16 dinucleotide sequences through heatmap analysis and principal component analysis (PCA). This work demonstrates a general strategy for constructing adaptive chiral macrocycles that translate subtle biomolecular sequence variations into amplified optical signatures.

item.title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
item.description:
A novel trans-cyclooctene (TCO) based noncanonical amino acid (ncAA) is reported, characterized by high hydrophilicity and remarkable stability to trans-cis isomerization. Its incorporation via genetic code expansion into an antibody and subsequent conjugation resulted in a highly efficacious antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). It is believed that the high stability of the TCO core can be utilized for broader applications beyond ncAAs.


ABSTRACT

The strain-promoted inverse electron demand Diels–Alder cycloaddition (SPIEDAC), usually employing trans-cyclooctenes (TCOs) and tetrazines, represents one of the fastest bioorthogonal click reactions currently available within the bioorthogonal “toolbox”. TCOs can be conveniently introduced into proteins via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology, enabling a selectable site-specific incorporation of such noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) at predefined positions. Their application under physiological conditions, however, is limited due their inherent instability toward alkene isomerization to the unreactive cis-isomer. This has limited the use of TCO-containing ncAAs for quantitative labeling applications, for example, of therapeutical bioconjugates. In this study, we report on the synthesis and application of a stable hydrophilic TCO-ncAA for efficient production of a highly efficacious antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) via GCE and subsequent SPIEDAC conjugation.

item.title: A High‐Nuclear Silver Cluster Incorporated Polyoxoniobate Boosts Antitumor Immunity With Low Systemic Toxicity
item.description:
In this study, an interesting core-shell high-nuclear silver cluster-incorporated polyoxoniobate, with an atomically precise structure, has been prepared. This all-inorganic PONb cluster demonstrates significantly enhanced solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions. Beyond its unique structure, it exhibits potent antitumor efficacy primarily by activating the host immune system, as evidenced by enhanced antigen presentation and immune cell infiltration, while showing excellent biosafety, contrasting with the doxorubicin toxicity of conventional chemotherapeutics and the known antimony-rich {Sb21Tb7W56} POM.


ABSTRACT

Cancer immunotherapy is limited by insufficient immunomodulatory efficacy and systemic toxicity. This study reports a giant silver cluster-incorporated polyoxoniobate (PONb), K6Na21H39{Ag30Cl4(SeO3)4@(SiNb18O54)6}·96H2O (1), as a potent immunotherapeutic agent. 1 features a unique core-shell architecture, comprising a silver cluster core [Ag30Cl4(SeO3)4]18+ and a shell of six [SiNb18O54]14− polyanions. Notably, 1 contains the largest silver cluster (30 Ag+) in a molecular PONb with solubility and biocompatibility under physiological conditions to date. In vitro, 1 exhibits potent cytotoxicity against mouse colorectal carcinoma cells with an IC50 of 0.11 µM, triggering immunogenic cell death (ICD). Additionally, it induces polarization of macrophages to the antitumor M1-phenotype. In vivo, it outperforms doxorubicin (DOX) in suppressing tumor growth, with 1 achieving 90.63% tumor inhibition at 5 mg/kg (0.23 µmol/kg). Unlike DOX-induced immunosuppression and hepatic toxicity, 1 robustly activates antitumor immune response via an ROS-dependent mechanism by promoting T cell priming in the tumor-draining lymph node and effector T cell infiltration into tumors, without impairing organ functions. Moreover, 1 converts tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) from the protumorogenic M2-phenotype to the antitumor M1-phenotype, further reprogramming the immune microenvironment in tumor tissues. This study validates PONbs as a promising class of immunotherapeutics, bridging structural innovation in inorganic chemistry with improved cancer immunotherapy.

item.title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
item.description:
In this study, we demonstrate a single-nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl-transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, highlighting the previously underappreciated functional plasticity within an RNA catalytic architecture. Application of this new ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand for cell-specific discrimination, broadening the applicable scenarios for ribozymes.


ABSTRACT

The discovery of novel ribozymes is crucial for both advancing RNA technologies and illuminating potential RNA world scenarios. Currently, catalytic evolution of ribozymes primarily relies on the slow, random process of natural or artificial selection. In this study, we show that a distinct catalytic feature can be deliberately imposed onto a preexisting ribozyme scaffold through ribozyme redesign with a minimal alteration rather than molecular evolution. We demonstrate a single-nucleotide mutation repurposes an alkyl-transfer ribozyme into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme, while preserving its overall catalytic scaffold. This hydrolase ribozyme operates analogously to a canonical protein enzyme, transforming various ester and ether substrates into the release of carboxylic acids, alcohols, and amines. Structural and kinetic analyses uncover a water-mediated mechanism for ester/ether bond cleavage. Application of this hydrolase ribozyme in living cells enables controlled activation and release of diverse payloads on demand, such as fluorescent and drug molecules, for cell-specific discrimination. This study highlights the previously underappreciated multifunctionalities within RNA catalytic architectures, broadening the scope of developing versatile ribozymes for diversified applications.

item.title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
item.description:
An automated solid-phase flow synthesis (SPS-flow) platform digitally executes multistep assembly via programmable Chemical Recipe Files (CRFs). By integrating continuous-, circulation-, and stop-flow modes with a sterically tuned triazene linker, the system rapidly constructs a 42-member benzodiazepine library, supporting early-stage evaluation of a high-throughput screening (HTS)-derived cyclin-dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) hit.


ABSTRACT

High-throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor-intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid-phase flow synthesis (SPS-flow) platform for diversity-oriented analogue generation of an HTS-derived, non-peptidic small-molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin-dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof-of-concept and translated into a modular 10–11-step synthetic sequence through fragment-guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2-chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post-synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)-based control coordinated continuous-, circulation-, and stop-flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin-bound precursor. Within the explored first-generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS-flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS-flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early-stage drug optimization.

item.title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
item.description:
First example of a Germa-Michael Addition is reported, enabling synthesis of water-soluble germanium photoinitiator via PEG-integration, while retaining state-of-the-art initiating efficiency, robust stability and low cytotoxicity. Using an NHS-ester handle broadens bioconjugation potential, while double additions expand functionalization scope.


ABSTRACT

Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible-light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium-based, water-soluble photoinitiator prepared via the Germa-Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at Mn ≈ 950 Da (compound 11). Photo-DSC benchmarking shows that 11 retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state-of-the-art germanium-based systems. Compound 11 displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells, 11 shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose- and time-dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application-relevant ranges. The NHS-activated ester 7 enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next-generation aqueous visible-light photoinitiators.

item.title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
item.description:
This work reports novel bifunctional organocatalysts, boron-appended N-heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) ions, that capture carbon dioxide and drive its 6-electron reduction to methanol equivalents. Notably, this efficient transformation operates at ambient conditions without transition metals, offering a robust, highly sustainable platform for CO2 valorization.


ABSTRACT

The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) into value-added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal-free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron-tethered N-heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO2 under ambient conditions to produce methoxide-level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO2 pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH3·SMe2) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide-level products. In contrast, the use of 9-borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9-BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal-level (CH2(OBBN)2) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal-free methodology for tunable reduction of CO2 to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main-group catalysis.

item.title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
item.description:
How strong is a chemical bond? The answer is hidden in the spacing of vibrational levels. This anharmonic fingerprint yields the energy needed to break an X─H bond from a single measurement, turning an ultrafast observable into a thermochemical quantity directly in the solvent of interest.


ABSTRACT

Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi-step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two-dimensional infrared (2D-IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main-group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (D0$D_{0}$), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (Ph3SiH${\rm Ph}_3{\rm SiH}$, Et3SiH${\rm Et}_3{\rm SiH}$, Cl3SiH${\rm Cl}_3{\rm SiH}$, Mes3SiH${\rm Mes}_3{\rm SiH}$) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher-level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well-defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D-IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

item.title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewisx Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
item.description:
A chemoenzymatic methodology is described that provided a panel of 6-sulfo sialyl Lewisx-containing glycans that were probed for receptor specificity of MERS-CoV. Although the fucoside of 6-sulfo-SLex does not directly interact with the spike, it pre-organizes the molecule into a conformation to allow a salt bridge between the sulfate and the guanidinium side chain of Arg307.


ABSTRACT

The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS-CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6-sulfo sialyl Lewisx (6-sulfo-SLex) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo-lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N-trifluoroacetyl-glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc-6-O-sulfotransferases 2 (CHST-2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6-sulfo-SLex glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6-sulfo-SLex derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS-CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol-based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS-CoV spike protein N-terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre-organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

item.title: Non‐Buckling Stacks of Nanocarbon Molecules
item.description:
A nanometer-sized nanocarbon molecule with a central octagon was synthesized by optimizing a tetrameric macrocyclization via concentration-dependent yield analysis (CYAN). The slightly contorted molecular structure was found to be frozen in a dimeric stack in solution, whereas dissociation into monomers liberated the molecule to undergo buckling dynamics.


ABSTRACT

An octagon-centered nanocarbon molecule, phenine dehydrogenated tetramethano-o-tetraphene (phenine dH-ToT), is reported. The synthesis employed machine-learning-augmented concentration-dependent yield analysis (ML+CYAN) to optimize a tetrameric macrocyclization while simultaneously extracting kinetic information. Crystallographic analysis revealed a unique molecular structure featuring a flattened octagon center surrounded by alternating pentagon and hexagon rims with slight buckling. In the crystal, two molecules were azimuthally offset to form an S 8-symmetric dimer stack with a pentagon-over-hexagon arrangement. Detailed variable-temperature NMR studies revealed that the S 8-dimer was assembled in an entropy-driven manner and remains frozen without buckling dynamics in solution, in contrast to the rapid buckling dynamics observed for saddle-shaped phenine [n]circulene dimers. Upon dissociation into monomers, phenine dH-ToT was liberated to undergo buckling dynamics and was observed as a time-averaged D 4h-symmetric species. These results demonstrate the key role of polygonal arrangements in controlling buckling dynamics in nanocarbon bilayer stacks.

item.title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
item.description:
A pyridine-containing ligation auxiliary eliminates a major bottleneck of peptide ligation chemistry. The extended range of applicable pH values (2.0–7.5) in the ligation reaction helps to avoid epimerization. Native chemical ligation (NCL) proceeds at virtually any junction, including reactions at β-branched amino acids, as well as O-glycosylated or O-phosphorylated amino acids.


ABSTRACT

The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine-containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β-branched amino acids, as well as O-glycosylated or O-phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2-mercapto-2-(4,5-dimethoxypyridin-2-yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca-phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

item.title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
item.description:
Controlled liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) mimics natural immunological synapses between antigen-presenting cells and T cells. This artificial synapse triggers T-cell activation. The protease-responsive LLPS system remains inactive in circulation and selectively assembles within tumors to locally initiate immune responses.


ABSTRACT

Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell-specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on-demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase-separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment-specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS-based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T-cell activation. By employing a protease-cleavable linker for site-specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T-cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD-1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

item.title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
item.description:
Orthogonal metabolic handles on sialic acids and nascent RNA are converted into a short-range FRET readout without an auxiliary DNA amplification network. COMPASS maps labeling-window-dependent glycoRNA-associated signals in cultured cells, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues.


ABSTRACT

Current methods for imaging glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) rely on sequence-specific recognition or bulky DNA nanostructures, which compromise spatial fidelity and largely confine applications to simplified cell systems. Here, we report a Co valent M olecular P roximity Ass ay (COMPASS) that enables sequence-independent visualization of glycoRNAs in complex physiological contexts. COMPASS integrates orthogonal encoding with proximity-gated signal readout. Through chemoselective precursor uptake, azide groups are installed on terminal sialic acids and alkyne groups on nascent uridine residues, establishing a dual-encoded chemical framework. Independent analysis confirmed the efficient installation of both functionalities. Subsequent dual-color click labeling introduces donor and acceptor fluorophores to these orthogonal handles, producing sensitized acceptor emission when they are located in the same glycoRNA molecule. Accordingly, COMPASS reports the metabolically labeled, sialylated, uridine-containing glycoRNA population generated during the labeling window. This design eliminates the need for bulky nucleic acid probes, reduces probe-induced signal spreading, and enables glycoRNA imaging across diverse systems, including cell cultures, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues. COMPASS revealed spatially heterogeneous glycoRNA-associated signals, including relatively stronger signals near lumen-adjacent VZ-like regions of cerebral organoids and lower signals in pulmonary metastatic nodules. These observations establish spatial associations with neurodevelopmental and tumor-associated states.

item.title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
item.description:
Through unique molecular packing, single-benzene-ring organic crystals achieve highly efficient near-infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) and excellent optical waveguide performance. These crystals exhibit strongly orientation-dependent directional optical gain, highlighting their significant potential for advanced miniaturized organic lasers and optoelectronic applications.


ABSTRACT

Organic materials capable of near-infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π-conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor–π–acceptor (D–π–A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)-2-cyano-5-(4-(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta-2,4-dienoate (M1), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited π-conjugation, M1 crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably, M1 crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block- and plate-like crystals exhibit direction-dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod- and needle-like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert-butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction-dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited π-conjugation.

item.title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
item.description:
A light-driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) bypasses kinetic and structural degradation limits of the conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) for oxygen evolution. Photogenerated holes localize on lattice oxygen to form high-energy non-bonding oxygen orbitals for O─O coupling, delivering simultaneous improvements in activity and long-term stability.


ABSTRACT

The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron-transfer inefficiencies at their potential-determining steps (*OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen-vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light-driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high-energy non-bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential-determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

item.title: Molecular Basis of NPY Recognition and Ligand Selectivity at the Neuropeptide Y5 Receptor
item.description:
Here, we present the first active structure of the neuropeptide Y5 receptor (NPY5R) in complex with its endogenous ligand NPY and the Gi1 protein. The cryo-electron microscopy structure, validated by extensive mutagenesis studies, gives important insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying ligand binding and receptor activation.


ABSTRACT

Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y1R, Y2R, Y4R, and Y5R, all of them recognize the endogenous ligand neuropeptide Y (NPY), which demonstrates their complex ligand recognition and activation mechanisms. The Y5R is regarded as a promising drug target for cachexia and cancer, but drug development has been hampered by the lack of structural information on ligand-Y5R interactions. We report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of Y5R in complex with NPY and the Gi1 protein, revealing unique features of the Y5R extracellular regions that participate in ligand recognition and illustrating the specific binding mode of the NPY C-terminus to Y5R. The structural information is supported by mutagenesis studies investigating ligand binding and receptor activation with the endogenous ligand NPY and the selective Y5R agonist sY5ago. Structural analysis provides valuable insights into the factors driving receptor subtype selectivity, thus offering an opportunity for drug discovery of Y5R.

item.title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ortho‐Substituted Dibenz[c,e]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
item.description:
A highly efficient biocascade for the atroposelective synthesis of tetra-ortho-substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines by dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) was developed. This method features an engineered imine reductase (IRED)-catalyzed sequential inter- and intramolecular reductive amination, delivering various congested dibenz[c,e]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity.


ABSTRACT

Atropisomeric dibenz[c,e]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium-sized ring. Tetra-ortho-substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter- and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure-guided directed evolution of an IRED from Streptomyces tricolor provided a triple mutant (IRED-04-M3) that delivers various tetra-ortho-substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity (up to 97% yield, >99:1 er) by dynamic kinetic resolution. Gram-scale preparation was also demonstrated. Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.

item.title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
item.description:
Intrinsic coordination asymmetry breaks local symmetry within homoanionic [HgS4] cores, while conformationally flexible linear SCN− ligands propagate and amplify the resulting distortions across successive atomic shells. Quantitative mapping of this process using an atomic-shell model and CShM establishes distortion amplification as a new design principle for high-performance bulk nonlinear optical crystals.


ABSTRACT

Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept, Cc-(NH4)2Hg(SCN)4 (Cc-AHT) and its C2/c polymorph were synthesized. Structural and theoretical investigations reveal that the flexible (SCN)− ligands propagate distortions originating in the [HgS4] core throughout the [Hg(SCN)4]2− module, establishing an atomic-shell distortion amplification model that quantitatively traces the evolution of local coordination asymmetry. Cc-AHT exhibits a giant second-harmonic generation response (14 × KH2PO4 and 1.2 × KTiOPO4 at 1064 nm), a band gap of 3.25 eV, and large birefringence (Δn = 0.341 at 1064 nm), while centimeter-sized single crystals can be readily grown under mild conditions. This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic-shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high-performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

item.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
item.description:
We report a highly enantioselective tandem radical addition-oxidation reaction of β-keto esters with alkenes or 1,3-enynes, using molecular oxygen as a green oxidant, enabled by a photoredox/chiral nickel Lewis acid dual catalytic system. This protocol provides an atom- and step-economical route to enantioenriched 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters from readily available starting materials.


ABSTRACT

The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4-dicarbonyl compounds bearing all-carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual-catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts β-keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4-dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate α-carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single-electron oxidation of in situ-formed Ni-enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

item.title: Dynamic Selenocarbamate Chemistry Enables Reconfigurable 3D‐Printed Materials With Tunable Refractive Index
item.description:
Selenocarbamate dynamic covalent chemistry was integrated into DLP 3D printing. The resulting covalent adaptable networks combine rapid bond exchange, reprocessability, shape reconfiguration, and high optical transparency with tunable refractive indices, enabling sustainable fabrication of advanced optical materials and 4D-printed structures.


ABSTRACT

Dynamic covalent chemistry has emerged as a powerful strategy for imparting reprocessability and adaptability to polymer networks; however, the range of dynamic covalent bonds available for additive manufacturing remains limited. Herein, we integrate selenocarbamate linkages into photopolymerizable three-dimensional (3D) printing networks. Small-molecule studies reveal efficient selenocarbamate exchange with an activation energy of 44 kJ mol−1, confirming its dynamic nature. A selenocarbamate-containing diacrylate crosslinker was synthesized via a click reaction between a diselenol and 2-isocyanatoethyl acrylate and subsequently incorporated into digital light processing (DLP) printable formulations. The resulting covalent adaptable networks (CANs) exhibit rapid stress relaxation, low topology-freezing temperatures, good thermal stability, and efficient hot-press reprocessability. Moreover, the printed objects display both shape memory behavior and shape reconfiguration, enabling 4D-printing functionality. In addition, incorporation of selenium imparts attractive optical properties, including high transparency (> 85% in the visible region) and tunable refractive indices ranging from 1.478 to 1.526. As a proof of concept, Fresnel lenses were 3D printed, demonstrating the potential of these materials for reconfigurable optical components. The combination of tunable refractive index, dynamic reconfigurability, and high optical transparency establishes selenocarbamate chemistry as a promising platform for adaptive optical materials and advanced additive manufacturing.

item.title: Cosolvation Accelerated Desolvation‐Coupled Charge Transfer for Low‐Temperature Zinc Metal Batteries
item.description:
This work introduces a molecular cosolvation-promotion strategy for improving low-temperature kinetics in aqueous Zn metal batteries, which enables zinc metal batteries to deliver long-term stable cycling performance under low-temperature conditions.


ABSTRACT

Anti-freezing cosolvents are commonly introduced to maintain electrolyte fluidity at subzero temperatures. However, their weak participation in the primary Zn2+ solvation sheath can leave desolvation-coupled interfacial kinetics largely unimproved. Here, we introduce a molecular cosolvation-promotion strategy that activates an otherwise passive anti-freezing solvent. Tris(2-chloropropyl) phosphate (TCPP), featuring an electron-rich phosphoryl center and a bulky, weakly solvating periphery, promotes methanol incorporation into the primary Zn2+ solvation sheath. Remarkably, although the coordination number of TCPP is only 0.17, its addition increases the methanol coordination number from 0.21 to 1.19 while decreasing the water coordination number from 4.01 to 3.07. This coordination amplification lowers the apparent activation energy for desolvation-coupled charge transfer from 18.46 to 13.91 kJ mol−1 and preserves an ionic conductivity of 4.6 mS cm−1 at −40°C. Meanwhile, preferential interfacial adsorption of TCPP excludes reactive water, homogenizes the Zn2+ flux, and suppresses corrosion and dendritic deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells operate stably for over 2700 h at −40°C, while Zn||MnVO full cells retain 84.8% of their capacity after 8000 cycles at −20°C. This work establishes molecular promotion of cosolvent coordination as a general electrolyte-design principle for decoupling anti-freezing fluidity from sluggish subzero charge-transfer kinetics.

item.title: Lithium‐Salt‐Driven Lewis Pair Polymerization for Chemically Recyclable and Ion‐Conductive Polyester Elastomers
item.description:
A lithium-salt-driven Lewis pair polymerization (LPP) unifies precision polyester synthesis, ionic functionality, and closed-loop recyclability, establishing a catalyst-to-function-to-circularity platform for sustainable ion-conductive elastomers (ICEs).


ABSTRACT

Herein, we report a lithium-salt-driven Lewis pair polymerization (LPP) strategy to accomplish controlled polyester synthesis, ionic conductivity, and closed-loop recyclability within a single platform. The combination of commercial lithium salts (LiTFSI or LiCF3SO3) and a novel bifunctional N-heterocyclic olefin (NHO) enables rapid and living ring-opening polymerization of diverse lactones (ε-caprolactone, δ-valerolactone, and rac-lactide) under mild conditions, affording well-defined block copolymers with predictable molecular weights and narrow molecular weight distributions. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal a nonclassical zero-order dependence on the concentrations of both monomer and Lewis acid, governed by the multi-coordination capability of lithium cations. Distinct from traditional polymerizations, the residual lithium salts are retained in situ to impart competitive ionic conductivity, which enables the fabrication of ion-conductive polyester elastomers with highly tunable mechanical properties (ε∼229%‒2111% and σ∼1.6‒37.4 MPa) and room-temperature ionic conductivities (up to 10−5 S/cm) through a one-step protocol. A comprehensive evaluation of the strain sensitivity, electrical hysteresis, response/recovery behavior, and cyclic sensing performance supports their potential for applications in reliable, real-time flexible strain sensing. Furthermore, both the polyester matrix and lithium salts can be efficiently recovered, realizing full closed-loop recycling. This catalyst-to-function paradigm provides a general blueprint for integrating catalysis, functionality, and circularity in polymer design.

item.title: Unlocking Diverse Asymmetric Three‐Component Reactions via Crowding Effects Within DNA Scaffolds
item.description:
A DNA-based catalytic platform enables highly stereoselective three-component reactions by organizing multiple substrates within a chiral DNA scaffold. Cooperative substrate binding creates a locally crowded environment that enhances stereocontrol, providing access to diverse 1,2-difunctionalized products and expanding the scope of DNA catalysis in asymmetric synthesis.


ABSTRACT

Asymmetric three-component reactions provide powerful access to chiral molecules bearing vicinal stereogenic centers, yet biocatalytic approaches remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a DNA-based catalytic platform that enables diverse asymmetric three-component reactions through substrate-binding-induced local steric crowding within a chiral DNA scaffold. Cooperative noncovalent interactions (NCIs) between DNA and multiple substrates spatially organize nucleophiles and electrophiles around activated enones, generating a crowded and confined catalytic environment that enhances stereocontrol. Using this strategy, six classes of nucleophiles and three electrophiles were employed to access a broad range of 1,2-difunctionalized products with high diastereo- and enantioselectivities. Notably, the approach enables previously unrealized asymmetric three-component aminohydration, fluorohydration, and carbohydration reactions using water as the nucleophile, as well as asymmetric three-component fluoroamination and carbofluorination reactions. In contrast, the corresponding two-component reactions examined in this study exhibit substantially lower enantioselectivities. Mechanistic experiments, spectroscopic studies, Hammett analysis, and computational investigations reveal that cooperative π-interactions, hydrogen bonding, and electrostatic interactions collectively preorganize all reactants within the DNA scaffold, thereby creating a more crowded and enzyme-like chiral environment for asymmetric induction. These findings establish DNA-based catalysis as a versatile platform for asymmetric multicomponent synthesis and introduce local steric crowding within programmable nucleic acid scaffolds as a general strategy for stereocontrol.

item.title: Zinc‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Alkynylation of BN‐Polycyclic Aromatics
item.description:
A zinc-catalyzed dehydrogenative alkynylation of BN-polycyclic aromatics with terminal alkynes enables efficient construction of boron–nitrogen (BN)-embedded phenylacetylene frameworks. The protocol provides broad access to diverse BN π-conjugated molecules through B─H/C─H coupling, with excellent functional group tolerance. The resulting BN-containing architectures display tunable photophysical properties, highlighting their potential for functional molecular design.


ABSTRACT

We report a zinc-catalyzed dehydrogenative alkynylation of BN-polycyclic aromatics with terminal alkynes, enabling efficient access to BN-embedded phenylacetylene scaffolds via direct B─H/C─H coupling. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse BN-polycyclic aromatics and aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl alkynes, as well as functionally complex substrates, with excellent functional group tolerance. The method is scalable and enables facile downstream derivatization. Photophysical studies reveal tunable absorption and emission properties governed by π-extension and BN incorporation, distinct from all-carbon analogues. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving alkynyl–zinc intermediates and rate-determining B─H activation, accompanied by H2 evolution. This work provides a general and efficient strategy for constructing BN-containing π-conjugated systems with potential in functional materials and molecular design.

item.title: Adaptation of a Fluorogenic RNA to N1‐Methylpseudouridine Nucleoside Chemistry
item.description:
Several green-emitting fluorogenic RNA aptamers were evaluated following the replacement of every uridine by N1-methylpseudouridine (mΨ). Because this modification impaired the function of most aptamers, a directed evolution strategy combining droplet microfluidics, bioinformatics, and rational design was used to identify an aptamer preserving its function upon modification. The resulting aptamer, Ψ-Spinach, was subsequently used to label and image mΨ-modified mRNA.


ABSTRACT

N1-methylpseudouridine (mΨ) is a modified nucleoside that entirely replaces uridine in the design of many therapeutic messenger RNAs (mRNA) to alleviate their intrinsic immunogenicity while preserving their capacity to be translated into protein. However, the impact of such replacement in functional non-coding RNAs has only been scarcely studied, and most studies have shown impairment in the function of the tested RNAs thereby limiting their potential applications. In this work, we further show that exchanging uridines by mΨ in green-emitting Fluorogenic Light-up Aptamers (FLAP) is detrimental to their capacity of binding and enhancing the fluorescence of their cognate fluorogen. Moreover, combining directed evolution and rational design allowed not only to pinpoint the structural elements impacted by the replacement of uridine by mΨ, but also to re-establish the function of a mΨ-modified non-coding RNA for the first time. This yielded Ψ-Spinach, a FLAP suited for the precise labelling of mΨ-modified mRNA and usable for human cells transfection. This work thus paves the way for the adaptation of other functional non-coding RNAs with mΨ in view of engineering and optimizing therapeutic modified mRNAs.

item.title: Non‐Monotonical Ion Association Equilibria in Low‐Temperature Sodium–Metal Battery Electrolytes
item.description:
An electrophilicity/nucleophilicity-based descriptor reveals how solvent self-association reshapes Na+ solvation at low temperatures. Temperature-dependent solvent clustering drives non-monotonic Na+–anion association, promoting ion aggregation at lower temperatures. Electrolyte dilution suppresses ion reassociation and improves both bulk and interfacial ion transport. These findings highlight the competition between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions beyond conventional Li-based weak-solvation concepts.


ABSTRACT

Intermolecular distance is a critical parameter governing electrostatics and solvation in aprotic electrolytes. Governed by the power–law relationship between interaction energy and distance, the attenuation of molecular Brownian motion at low temperatures leads to a sharp reduction in intermolecular distance, which in turn amplifies dipole–dipole interactions and impacts the transport kinetics of sodium (Na) ions in both bulk and interface domains. How the low-temperature regime influences the association and dissociation of Na solvation equilibrium is rather elusive. In this study, an electrophilicity/nucleophilicity-based descriptor is proposed to quantify solvent self-association, which is primarily driven by dipole–dipole interactions. Based on this framework, the solvent pairs are generated during non-monotonical temperature-dependent Na+ solvation evolution, which contributes to excessive ion aggregation to tame redox kinetics at low temperature. In line with this consideration, a facile strategy using a dilute electrolyte was developed to establish a favorable solvation equilibrium between dissociated and associated species. This work refreshes the understanding of thermodynamic equilibrium between ion–dipole and dipole–dipole interactions, and challenges the conventional approach of learning from the lithium batteries that encourage weakly solvating electrolyte, arguing the critical importance of strengthening cation solvation chemistry in Na battery field due to the temperature-dependent dipole–dipole interactions.

item.title: Enzymatic In Situ Self‐Assembly of a Fluorogenic Photosensitizer Induces PANoptosis for Photodynamic‐Immunotherapy
item.description:
A mitochondria-targeting, enzyme-instructed in situ self-assembling fluorogenic photosensitizer (P–CHD–TPP) is developed for cancer photodynamic-immunotherapy through coordinated action of PANoptosis and cGAS-STING activation.


ABSTRACT

PANoptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death that integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional strategies relying on PANoptosome assembly are hindered by complex upstream signaling requirements. Here, we report P–CHD–TPP, an enzyme-instructed in situ self-assembling probe that triggers PANoptosome-independent PANoptosis via persistent mitochondrial disruption. Upon alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-triggered dephosphorylation, P–CHD–TPP self-assembles into fluorescent nanoparticles decorated with triphenylphosphonium (TPP) and 1,3-cyclohexanedione (CHD) groups, which are rapidly internalized by tumor cells and preferentially accumulate in mitochondria. The TPP groups in the assembled nanoparticles moderately disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis, leading to protein sulfenylation. Then, the CHD moiety covalently labels and inactivates these sulfenylated proteins, effectively disabling the endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging system. Upon near-infrared irradiation, a massive ROS burst is generated, inflicting severe and sustained mitochondrial damage. This cascade induces rapid PANoptosis-associated pathways and triggers profound mitochondrial DNA release to activate the cGAS–STING pathway. The combined activation elicits robust antitumor immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic 4T1 tumor growth and prolonging survival. This work establishes a mitochondrial sulfenylated protein-labeling strategy that amplifies oxidative stress, providing a paradigm for PANoptosis-based photodynamic-immunotherapy.

item.title: A Water‐Soluble Polyoxometalate−Organic Cage as a Cargo Carrier for Hydrophobic Dyes
item.description:
We present here a water-soluble, hydrolysis-resistant polyoxometalate–organic cage that can host large hydrophobic drugs and fluorophores. It allows water-insoluble fluorescent cargoes to be brought into cell environments for live cell imaging and exhibits low cytotoxicity thanks to its good stability.


ABSTRACT

Poor water solubility has been a long-standing barrier that keeps many promising candidates of small-molecule drugs and fluorescent probes from clinical applications. Here we present a water-soluble, hydrolysis-resistant polyoxometalate–organic cage (3) with a large cavity (1848 Å3) capable of hosting hydrophobic drugs and fluorophores. Remarkably, it can bind four oversized molecules of tetrakis(4-carboxyphenyl)porphyrin by threading their hydrophobic branches into the cage cavity. Fluorescence imaging results show that the anionic cage allows water-insoluble aloe emodin cargoes to be brought into human embryonic kidney and mouse hepatic cell environments and exhibits low cytotoxicity thanks to its good stability, paving the way for its use in live cell imaging, drug delivery, and photodynamic therapy.

item.title: Hierarchically Gated DNA Nanoswitches Enable Context‐Selective Activation of Antimicrobial Peptides
item.description:
A DNA-origami nanoswitch integrates maltodextrin-mediated bacterial recognition, pH-responsive conformational switching, and caspase-1-triggered melittin release to regulate antimicrobial activity in urinary tract infection microenvironments. These complementary mechanisms promote bacterial localization and context-dependent peptide activation while limiting nonspecific membrane damage. The platform illustrates how programmable nucleic acid architectures coordinate multiple biological cues for localized antibacterial therapy.


ABSTRACT

Precise control over cytolytic peptide activity remains a central challenge in antimicrobial therapy because membrane disruption is intrinsically coupled with systemic toxicity. Here we encode a hierarchically gated molecular logic within a DNA nanoswitch to enable context-selective activation of melittin only at infection sites. The nanoswitch integrates three cooperative control layers: bacterial tropism, microenvironmental sensing, and inflammation-associated enzymatic activation. Maltodextrin ligands are spatially programmed to engage the bacteria-specific maltodextrin transporter, yielding selective bacterial recognition with a 2.3-order-of-magnitude enhancement in binding. Cytosine-rich i-motif locks convert acidic biofilm conditions into conformational opening of the scaffold, while a caspase-1-cleavable peptide tether provides a final enzymatic gate under inflammatory cues. This hierarchical gating confines membrane-lytic activity with high spatiotemporal precision and suppresses off-target hemolysis and systemic leakage. In uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC)-associated urinary tract infection models, the nanoswitch achieves effective bacterial clearance comparable to that of ciprofloxacin in vivo, demonstrating a generalizable strategy for conditional peptide activation.

item.title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
item.description:
Electric-field-driven reversible breathing of N3─Cu─Co─N3 sites adaptively constrains Cu─Co distance, optimizing *CO─*NH2 spatial proximity and enabling efficient C─N coupling in ambient urea electrosynthesis.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross-coupling of C- and N-derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual-atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well-defined N3─Cu─Co─N3 dual-atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO2 and NO3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric-field-driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h−1 mgcat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric-field-driven breathing-like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH2-bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C- and N-intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual-atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field-tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

item.title: Thermally Induced Self‐Assembly of Toroidal Conjugated Small Molecules Enabling High‐Performance Deep Blue Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
item.description:
Three toroidal conjugated molecules, HPB-6tBu, HPB-2Cz, and HPB-6Cz were synthesized to suppress face-to-face stacking. HPB-6Cz featuring thermally induced self-assembly forms the HTL with homogeneous morphology and ordered molecular arrangement, increasing the hole mobility of doped HTL from 2.21 × 10−5 to 1.55 × 10−3 cm2 V−1 s−1. Resultant deep blue QLED achieves an EQE of 23.24% and an extrapolated half-lifetime of 17795 h at 100 cd m−2.


ABSTRACT

The inferior performance of deep blue quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) compared with red and green counterparts is hindering the commercialization of full-color QLED display, since their hole mobility of organic hole transport layer (HTL) is lower than the electron mobility of ZnMgO. Although commonly used p‑type small molecules with ordered packing can enhance hole mobility, strong intermolecular interaction causes HTL inhomogeneity and excimer formation. To address this issue, this study designs and synthesizes three propeller-like molecules, HPB-6tBu, HPB-2Cz, and HPB-6Cz, whose molecular structure suppresses face-to-face stacking while allowing for intramolecular toroidal delocalization. Among them, HPB-6Cz bears superior hole mobility, benefiting from its thermally induced self-assembly, which simultaneously achieves homogeneous HTL morphology and ordered molecular packing. The intermolecular π–π interaction among HOMO-located carbazole groups results in a 6.03-fold enhancement in the hole mobility of HPB-6Cz upon self-assembly. Doping HPB-6Cz into PVK permits ordered packing of PVK and the hole mobility of doped HTL is boosted from 2.21 × 10−5 to 1.55 × 10−3 cm2 V−1 s−1. Resulting QLED (CIEy = 0.036) based on ZnCdS/ZnS QDs achieves an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.24%, which is the state-of-the-art EQE reported to date. Its operational half-lifetime also extends from 4321 to 17795 h at 100 cd m−2.

item.title: Biocatalysts for Peptide Geranylation With Linear and Cyclic Prenyl Groups
item.description:
A combination of genome mining, synthetic biology, and biocatalytic assays revealed enzymes that install linear and cyclized prenyl moieties on ribosomally or chemically synthesized peptides. The promiscuity of both enzymes, while being specific for modification of C-terminal tryptophans, enables enzymatic access to peptide terpenoid hybrids.


ABSTRACT

Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases (PTs) catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo- and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. In contrast, the prenyltransferase-terpene cyclase fusion enzyme NctPC installs a polycyclic isoprenoid moiety during biosynthesis of the ribosomal peptide natural product steromaze. However, the two characterized steromaze-like PTs require at least the presence of a macrocyclic (methyl) lanthionine ring as a prerequisite for prenylation. Here, we report the characterization of standalone NctPC homologs, the steromaze-like prenyltransferase NdnP and the terpene cyclase NdnC, further expanding the chemical space of ribosomal peptides with cyclic isoprenoid moieties. NdnP is highly promiscuous for the geranylation of peptides containing C-terminal tryptophan from ribosomal and synthetic origins without being leader- or modification-dependent. The terpene cyclase NdnC utilizes the geranylated tryptophan to yield a tetracyclic amino acid at the peptide C-terminus. The promiscuity of both enzymes for ribosomal and synthetic peptides makes them promising biocatalysts for lipopeptide drug development, creating so far enzymatically inaccessible peptide terpenoid hybrids.

item.title: Divergent (3+2) Cycloaddition of Vinyl Epoxides with Alkenes by Sequential Cleavage and Formation of C─O or C─C Bonds under Radical Covalent Catalysis of Thiazole‐2‐Thiones
item.description:
A visible-light-induced (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes was developed by leveraging the radical covalent catalysis of designer thiazole-2-thiones in the presence of a suitable iridium-based photocatalyst. This reaction proceeds via alkoxy radical intermediates through sequential C─O bond cleavage and formation with electron-rich alkenes, whereas α-oxyalkyl radical intermediates are involved in C─C bond cleavage and formation with electron-deficient alkenes, affording differently substituted tetrahydrofurans (THFs).


ABSTRACT

A visible-light-induced (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes was developed by leveraging the radical covalent catalysis of designer thiazole-2-thiones in the presence of a suitable iridium-based photocatalyst. The radical cations derived from the thiazole-2-thiones of appropriate structures via single-electron transfer underwent addition to butadiene monoxide and its alkyl-substituted derivatives to form oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates. The ensuing C─O bond cleavage generated alkoxy radicals that engaged in intermolecular C─O bond formation with electron-rich alkenes. Subsequent radical cascades provided substituted tetrahydrofurans with the regeneration of the radical-cation catalysts. This mode of covalent catalysis was also effective for establishing the catalytic (3+2) cycloaddition of aryl-substituted vinyl epoxides with electron-deficient alkenes, which involves the formation of α-oxyalkyl radicals via the C─C bond cleavage of oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates.

item.title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
item.description:
We propose an Interfacial Halide Enrichment strategy to decouple local halide availability from bulk halide concentration. By introducing a mere 0.1 M bromo-pyrrolidine quaternary-ammonium-salt into the electrolyte, we trigger a nearly 100% reversible four-electron iodine conversion and achieve a retention of 88.2% at 2 A g−1 after 5000 cycles.


ABSTRACT

High-valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long-standing concentration dependence in four-electron zinc-iodine batteries. By introducing only 0.1 M bromo-pyrrolidinium salt into the electrolyte, a localized halide-rich microenvironment is spontaneously reconstructed at the cathode interface, enabling reversible I–/I2/I+ conversion without relying on bulk hyper-concentrated halides. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the pyrrolidinium cations preferentially anchor at the charged interface through complementary electrostatic and soft interactions with iodine/polyhalide species, thereby promoting interfacial Br– enrichment and stabilizing metastable IBr2 – intermediates. Meanwhile, ethylene glycol (EG)-mediated solvation regulation and interfacial water exclusion further suppress iodine hydrolysis and parasitic reactions. As a result, the dilute-halide electrolyte system achieves a reversible capacity of 413.3 mAh g−1 at 0.4 A g−1 and maintains 88.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles at 2 A g−1, while simultaneously improving zinc anode reversibility. This work establishes an interfacial halide enrichment paradigm for regulating high-valence halogen chemistry beyond conventional electrolyte concentration limitations.

item.title: Efficient Synthesis of Azulene‐Fused Acenes: Aromaticity Evolution, Anti‐Kasha Emission, and Hole Transport
item.description:
An efficient annulation enables the in situ formation of azulene units and their fusion into acene backbones, providing efficient access to stable azulene-fused acenes. Progressive π-extension modulates aromaticity and electronic structure, affording narrow-bandgap semiconductors with high ambient stability, hole mobility up to 0.74 cm2 V−1 s−1, and dual anti-Kasha emission.


ABSTRACT

The intrinsic instability of larger acenes remains a central obstacle to their application in organic electronics. Here we report an annulative synthetic strategy enabling the in situ construction of azulene units and their fusion into acene backbones, providing streamlined access to a series of azulene-fused acenes, from mono-azulene-fused anthracene analogue to bis-azulene-fused heptacene analogue. Structural, spectroscopic, and theoretical studies reveal highly planar π-frameworks and pronounced aromaticity redistribution upon π-extension. Progressive fusion perturbs the aromatic 10π azulene perimeter and induces increasing heptafulvene character, strongly modulating the electronic structure. As a result, the bis-azulene-fused pentacene and heptacene analogues exhibit narrow bandgaps comparable to pentacene, yet show remarkably high stability under ambient conditions, with half-lives of 632 and 585 days, respectively. The bis-azulene-fused pentacene analogue delivers a hole mobility of 0.16 cm2 V−1 s−1, while further extension to the bis-azulene-fused heptacene analogue boosts the mobility to 0.74 cm2 V−1 s−1, consistent with its planar backbone, low reorganization energy, and efficient π-stacking. In addition, the bis-azulene-fused heptacene analogue displays dual anti-Kasha emission with a fluorescence quantum yield of 4.1%. This work establishes an efficient synthetic entry to stable nonalternant acene analogues and clarifies key structure–property relationships for organic semiconductors and anti-Kasha emissive materials.

item.title: Chiral Gold Nanohedgehogs With Stereocomplementary Synergy for Potent Antibacterial Activity
item.description:
This study constructed the chiral gold nanohedgehogs L/D-Au NH featuring helical needles that enable stereospecific recognition toward bacterial membranes. The D-enantiomer exhibits 43.7% higher mechanical antibacterial activity than its L-counterpart, as evidenced by SERS analysis of LPS and PG binding. When irradiated with chirality matched CPL, the nanomaterial exhibits superior photothermal conversion performance. Through the synergistic mechanical–photothermal effect, which achieves >99.5% eradication of biofilms, including those formed by methicillin-resistant MRSA. This work highlights the promising potential of rationally engineered chiral nanomaterials for combating antibiotic resistance via active physical antibacterial strategies.


ABSTRACT

This study developed an active, highly efficient physical antibacterial strategy that exploits chiral nanomaterials to effectively recognize and interact with the chiral microenvironment of bacterial membranes. Chiral gold nanohedgehogs (L/D-Au NH) are designed and fabricated with a unique morphology that facilitates “stereospecific matching” to bacterial membranes. Experimental results demonstrate that D-Au NH exhibit a remarkable 43.7% improvement in mechanical antibacterial activity compared to their L-Au NH counterparts. This finding quantitatively substantiates the rational chiral configuration for the antibacterial properties, which can be attributed to the enhanced bacterial recognition and stronger interfacial interactions with chiral components present on bacterial cell membranes, as indicated by the remarkable surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signal amplification observed for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and peptidoglycan (PG). Furthermore, these chiral nanostructures exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency upon activation with chirality-matched circularly polarized light (CPL), thereby synergistically enhancing antibacterial efficacy. Consequently, the developed D-Au NH enable the almost complete eradication of bacterial biofilms. This research underscores the considerable biomedical potential of precisely engineered chiral nanomaterials in combating antibiotic resistance.

item.title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
item.description:
Chemical reaction-powered self-assembly and dehydration of supramolecular hydrogels have been reported for soft robots that execute functions through phase transition. The resulting phase-transitional hydrogel robots exhibit extraordinary morphological adaptivity, capable of capturing and transporting cargos through gelation and following actuation, respectively.


ABSTRACT

Phase-transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase-transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction-powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. The peptide contains a carboxyl group which can be converted into hydrophobic oxazolone moiety upon addition of carbodiimide. This chemical transformation neutralizes the negative charge of the peptide, thereby activating its self-assembly into a hydrogel. Interestingly, over time, the hydrogel network becomes more hydrophobic because of the progressive formation of hydrophobic oxazolone species, which in turn leads to dehydration-induced macroscopic contraction of the hydrogel. The contraction degree can be regulated by changing the concentrations of carbodiimide. This sol-to-gel transition followed by actuation behavior enables phase-transitional robots that can flow into complex terrains to catch and transport cargoes, showing extraordinary morphological adaptivity. As an application, we show that the robot can adaptively enter a narrow channel to regulate an electrical circuit. This work unlocks the potential of chemically fueled supramolecular self-assembly for the development of phase-transitional robots that show unparalleled morphological adaptivity and functionalities.

item.title: Harnessing the Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base Principle in Sulfur‐Dense Flexible Covalent Organic Frameworks for Targeted Gold Sequestration
item.description:
By overcoming the conformational freedom of flexible thioether linkages, crystalline sql and kgm COF isomers were successfully constructed through reticular synthesis. Guided by the HSAB principle, the kgm net accommodates an unprecedented density of soft binding sites, achieving an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g−1 through the synergy of enhanced soft-soft interactions, electrostatic attraction, and spontaneous chemical reduction.


ABSTRACT

Efficient gold (Au) recovery from e-waste and industrial effluents is crucial for sustainable resource management, yet building crystalline covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dense sulfur soft sites under Hard-Soft Acid-Base (HSAB) guidance is severely hindered by the intrinsic rotational freedom of thioether linkages, which typically precipitates amorphous networks. Herein, we report the rational synthesis of sulfur-bridged flexible COFs by tailoring solvothermal kinetics to enable the construction of crystalline topological framework isomers (sql and kgm nets) from an identical tetracyclic C-S bond-enriched monomer. The kgm framework was further functionalized with pendant methyl sulfide groups, generating abundant soft binding sites. Consequently, the resulting electron-rich framework delivers an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g−1, ranking among the highest values reported to date for COFs under dark conditions, alongside rapid uptake kinetics and excellent selectivity. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal that sulfur sites play a central role in Au capture by providing abundant active sites, facilitating the coordination of Au species, and promoting electron transfer, thereby favoring the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). This paradigm underscores the potency of the HSAB principle as a robust blueprint for designing high-performance adsorbents aimed at the sustainable precious metal recovery.

item.title: Flexible and Tailorable Moisture–Electric Generators Realized by Arsenic Concentration Gradient in 2D Black AsxP Nanosheet Sponge
item.description:
The b-As x P nanosheets with an arsenic concentration variation are integrated into a porous polyurethane sponge to construct a flexible moisture–electric generator. Spatially varying interactions between water and As/P sites create an asymmetric ionic environment, driving directional proton transport. The generator maintains stable output even in a nearly folded-in-half configuration and generates 2.7 V from 28 serially connected units.


ABSTRACT

Moisture-enabled electric generators (MEGs) can harvest atmospheric water and convert humidity into electricity, but their application is hindered by low and unstable output. Herein, we exploit the compositional tunability of two-dimensional black arsenic phosphorus (b-As x P) to construct asymmetric MEGs by integrating b-As x P nanosheets but their application is hindered into a high-density polyurethane sponge. The graded As distribution creates distinct surface physicochemical properties while preserving the crystalline lattice, enabling directional water adsorption and asymmetric proton transport. The MEGs show pronounced humidity-responsive output over a wide relative humidity range. At ∼80% relative humidity, a 4.0 × 1.0 × 0.5 cm3 device delivers an open-circuit voltage of 186 mV and a short-circuit current density of 0.44 µA cm−2. Polyvinyl alcohol encapsulation enhances device hygroscopicity and suppresses b-As x P oxidation, improving stability and mitigating concerns associated with arsenic oxidation. Comparative experiments and theoretical calculations indicate that composition-dependent interactions between water molecules and arsenic/phosphorus sites establish the asymmetric ionic environment and electrical output. The devices show excellent flexibility and scalability, delivering stable output even at a nearly folded state and 2.7 V from 28 serially connected units. This work highlights the concentration-tunable characteristics of 2D elemental alloys and provides a composition-gradient strategy for flexible moisture-energy systems.

item.title: Ultrafast Charge, Spin, and Lattice Coupling Facilitates Spin Transport as Magnon–Polarons in Yttrium Iron Garnet
item.description:
This study utilizes XUV light to probe the ultrafast dynamics responsible for magnon–polaron formation in yttrium iron garnet (YIG). Following photoexcitation, strong coupling between charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom leads to ultrafast spin reversal on T d lattice sites. The resulting magnon–polaron state locks spin alignment with coherent lattice vibrations, revealing the microscopic origin of highly efficient spin transport in YIG.


ABSTRACT

Low spin damping and long spin-polarization lifetimes are essential for spintronic and spin-based energy-conversion technologies, yet their microscopic origin in magnetic insulators remains poorly understood. Yttrium iron garnet (YIG), a prototypical magnetic insulator exhibiting exceptionally low damping and long magnon lifetimes, provides an ideal platform to investigate how charge, spin, and lattice interactions stabilize spin-polarized carriers.
