Here, we directly probe these coupled dynamics using ultrafast linearly and circularly polarized extreme-ultraviolet (XUV) spectroscopy, which provides femtosecond time resolution together with element- and site-specific sensitivity to electronic structure and spin polarization. Our measurements reveal the ultrafast formation of magnon–polaron quasiparticles mediated by strong charge–spin–lattice coupling. XUV magnetic circular dichroism (XUV-MCD) directly resolves a transient spin reversal at the Fe tetrahedral (T d ) site on the sub-picosecond timescale, removing the Pauli blocking that initially inhibits electron delocalization and thereby enabling efficient spin-polarized transport. Coherent charge–lattice dynamics and phonon coherence transfer further indicate the formation of delocalized quasiparticles extending over several to tens of unit cells. These results establish a direct microscopic link between magnon–polaron formation, the long-lived spin polarization and efficient spin transport in YIG, providing a framework for understanding how coupled spin–charge–lattice excitations govern spin transport in magnetic insulators.

item.title: Redox‑Gated Molecular Switching of CO2 Self‑Poisoning on Quinone Electrocatalysts Enables In Situ Self‑Regeneration
item.description:
CO2 is not merely a mineralization product: at reduced quinone sites, it forms carbonate adducts that poison 2e− oxygen reduction. A redox-gated pulsed electrocatalysis strategy periodically reoxidizes quinone sites to release bound CO2 in situ, boosting degradation kinetics and sustaining metal-free electrocatalytic water purification.


ABSTRACT

Quinone-based metal-free electrocatalysts offer a sustainable route for oxygen activation and water purification, yet their persistent activity decay has remained poorly understood. Here, we identify mineralization-derived CO2 as the major cause of a previously overlooked self-poisoning pathway in quinone‑based electrocatalysts: CO2 accumulates at the electrode–electrolyte interface and forms stable carbonate adducts with reduced quinone moieties, blocking the active sites for two-electron oxygen reduction to H2O2 and consequently suppressing ·OH generation through the cascade oxygen-reduction pathway. Electrochemical analysis further reveals that CO2 adduction reorganizes the native quinone redox transitions into potential-dependent carbonate-bound states, allowing the occupied quinone centers to be reversibly regenerated by oxidative pulses. Leveraging this principle, we developed a pulsed electrocatalytic strategy that periodically reoxidizes the quinone catalyst in situ, dynamically reversing CO2 poisoning without requiring chemical regenerants or thermal treatment. Across structurally diverse pollutants at neutral pH, this strategy accelerates degradation kinetics by up to 725.3% and retains up to 93.6% of its 2 h diclofenac removal efficiency after 12 h of continuous operation. More broadly, the redox-gated CO2 switching mechanism provides a generalizable design paradigm for mitigating CO2-induced deactivation in electrocatalytic systems prone to local CO2 buildup, including CO2 electrolysis, electrosynthetic biomass conversion, and electrochemical nitrogen fixation.

item.title: Tetraxene: Serendipity Leads to a Versatile Three‐Dimensional Building Block
item.description:
A serendipitous discovery is transformed into a rational synthetic strategy providing concise access to tetraxene, a versatile 3D COT-based building block. Its distinctive non-benzenoid architecture, unusual crystal packing, and orthogonally addressable reactive sites reveal a robust platform for the design of increasingly complex carbon-based molecular architectures.


ABSTRACT

Cyclooctatetraene (COT)-containing building blocks occupy a unique position in carbon materials, yet their synthesis generally relies on lengthy and low-yielding approaches. In this study, we report the serendipitous discovery and rational development of tetraxene, a synthetically accessible tetraindene-fused COT scaffold uncovered during attempts to extend truxene π-conjugation. Although indanone condensations intrinsically favor thermodynamically reinforced trimer formation, stepwise interception and reactivation of a discrete dimer intermediate redirects the reaction toward selective tetramerization. This two-step strategy provides concise access to a family of tetraxene derivatives (2b–e) in synthetically useful yields (70%–80%). Single-crystal x-ray diffraction reveals a rigid nonaromatic COT core with pronounced bond localization while demonstrating that subtle peripheral modifications profoundly alter solid-state symmetry, leading to remarkably diverse supramolecular architectures. Beyond its distinctive structural behavior, tetraxene contains orthogonally addressable reactive domains that enable modular functionalization at both the aromatic periphery and the five-membered rings. These results establish tetraxene as a structurally defined and chemically versatile 3D COT-based building block and demonstrate that thermodynamically biased aromatic condensation pathways can be deliberately redirected toward higher-order non-benzenoid carbon architectures.

item.title: From Lying to Standing: Anchoring Naphthoquinone via Pd─S Bonds on Pd Nanoclusters to Suppress Over‐Hydrogenation for Mild H2O2 Synthesis
item.description:
From lying to standing, Pd─S anchoring constrains naphthoquinone in an upright geometry on Pd nanoclusters, minimizing direct contact between the aromatic π-system and Pd while preserving efficient H2 activation. The resulting PdL/XC-72 catalyst delivers an H2O2 productivity of 300 mmol gPd −1 h−1 with stable cycling under mild conditions, demonstrating conformational control as an effective strategy for suppressing quinone over-hydrogenation.


ABSTRACT

The industrial anthraquinone (AQ) process for H2O2 production is limited by undesired deep hydrogenation of quinone working compound, promoted by cofacial adsorption of its aromatic π-system on Pd surfaces. Here, we report a Pd─S anchoring strategy that constrains a dithiolated naphthoquinone ligand (SNQ), whose quinone moiety serves as a simplified structural model of AQ, in a standing configuration on low-valent Pd nanoclusters. This directional coordination minimizes direct contact between the aromatic framework and Pd while retaining access of the carbonyl groups to activated hydrogen. Supported on XC-72 affords a catalyst that produces H2O2 through sequential H2 hydrogenation and air oxidation under mild conditions (0.2 MPa H2, 30°C), achieving 300 mmol gPd −1 h−1 and maintaining its initial activity over eight cycles. X- ray absorption spectroscopy supports the coexistence of Pd─Pd and Pd─S coordination, whereas in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals a reversible quinone/hydroquinone-type redox cycle. Density functional theory calculations further identify carbonyl hydrogenation as energetically favored over aromatic-ring hydrogenation. The Pd─S interface thus electronically promotes H2 activation and geometrically restricts the quinone π-system, spatially decoupling H2 activation from aromatic-ring adsorption and enabling selective, durable quinone-mediated H2O2 synthesis.

item.title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
item.description:
Organic solvent-free lipid nanoparticles featuring PEtOx-based stealth lipids enable efficient mRNA and CRISPR-Cas9 delivery while exhibiting markedly improved biocompatibility compared with PEG-based analogues. Their successful ex vivo and in vivo performance, combined with data-driven formulation optimization, establishes a versatile platform that addresses key limitations of conventional LNPs and advances sustainable nucleic acid delivery.


ABSTRACT

Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR-Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent-free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)-based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx-lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG-based analogues (12-fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR-Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80+ macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx-based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol-based production processes.

item.title: Polyacetylene‐Decorated Pt/TiO2 Catalyst for Highly Selective Hydrogenation of Alkynes
item.description:
A high-performance Pt/TiO2-200C2H2 catalyst featuring both Pt NPs and Pt SAs as dual active sites was fabricated via a simple and mild C2H2 pretreatment. The resulting PA coating on the catalyst surface donates electrons to the Pt sites, promoting H2 dissociation and activation and inhibiting sintering and aggregation of the Pt species, thus dramatically enhancing the catalytic activity and stability toward the hydrogenation of various alkynes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further demonstrate that the PA coating increases the hydrogenation barrier of styrene over Pt SAs and Pt NPs, thereby suppressing over-hydrogenation and enhancing selectivity.


ABSTRACT

Supported Pt nanoparticles (NPs) and Pt single atoms (SAs) are widely employed in the selective hydrogenation of various fine chemicals, where Pt NPs typically deliver high activity while Pt SAs afford exceptional selectivity. Integrating these advantages into a unified catalytic system to reconcile the trade-off between activity and selectivity in alkynes hydrogenation remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel Pt/TiO2-200C2H2 catalyst featuring both Pt NPs and Pt SAs active sites was prepared via a simple and mild C2H2 pretreatment. The C2H2 monomer undergoes polymerization to form trans-polyacetylene (PA), which in situ covers the surface of Pt NPs and Pt SAs. The PA coating on the Pt/TiO2-200C2H2 surface donates electrons to Pt sites, promoting H2 dissociation and activation, inhibiting sintering and aggregation of the Pt species, thereby significantly enhancing the catalytic activity and stability toward the hydrogenation of various alkynes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations prove that the PA coating increases the hydrogenation barrier of styrene on both Pt NPs and Pt SAs, suppressing over-hydrogenation and enhancing selectivity. This work not only offers a novel approach for fabrication of Pt-based dual active site catalysts but also presents a scalable polymer coating for modulating the catalytic performance of alkynes hydrogenation catalysts.

item.title: Gradient Mg and Uniform Ti Co‐Doping Suppresses Jahn–Teller Effect in LMFP via Optimized Ion‐Transport Kinetics and Interfacial Reactions
item.description:
A novel Mg/Ti co-doped Li0.98Mg0.02[(Mn0.6Fe0.4)0.98Ti0.02]0.98PO4 (Mg/Ti-LMFP) was synthesized via a wet–dry method, achieving consistent and gradual doping. Uniform Ti doping stabilizes the lattice, while gradient Mg enriches at the surface to form a protective layer, thereby preserving both bulk and interfacial stability. Compared with conventional LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4, Mg/Ti-LMFP strikes a balance between electrical conductivity and structural stability, effectively reducing the Jahn–Teller effect.


ABSTRACT

LiMn0.6Fe0.4PO4 (LMFP), an olivine-type cathode material, is gaining attention in high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries due to its high operating voltage and cost-effectiveness. However, its practical use is limited by slow Li+ diffusion, poor electronic conductivity, and structural degradation caused by Jahn–Teller distortion from Mn3+. To tackle these challenges, we have developed a dry-and-wet synthesis method to produce Mg/Ti co-doped LMFP (Mg/Ti-LMFP). This approach ensures uniform Ti4+ doping at Fe sites and gradient Mg2+ doping at Li sites. Ti4+ strengthens the structural stability by forming M─O bonds, reducing Jahn–Teller distortion. Additionally, surface-enriched Mg2+ creates a protective layer, preventing manganese dissolution and electrolyte decomposition. The optimized structure and chemistry enhance Li+ transport kinetics, stability, electronic conductivity, and cycling durability. Mg/Ti-LMFP demonstrates 88.7% capacity retention after 200 cycles at 1C (25°C) and 88.2% after 100 cycles at 1C (55°C). This study lays a solid foundation for designing high-performance co-doped olivine-type cathode materials, guiding the development of future energy storage solutions.

item.title: Chemical Inhibition of Pyocyanin Biosynthesis Attenuates Virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
item.description:
Anti-virulence strategies disarm pathogens rather than killing them directly. A β-lactone reduces pyocyanin production without affecting growth. Chemical proteomics identified PqsC as the primary target via binding to Cys129. Crystallography revealed the binding mode, and SAR yielded a chloroacetamide inhibitor with improved enzymatic potency and anti-virulence effects in mammalian cells.


ABSTRACT

Anti-virulence strategies that disarm bacterial pathogenicity without affecting viability offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics by reducing selective pressure for resistance. However, in Gram-negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the double-layered cell envelope limits intracellular access of small-molecule inhibitors. Here, we screened a structurally diverse library of virulence inhibitors, previously established as pathoblockers in Gram-positive bacteria, and identified a potent β-lactone inhibitor of pyocyanin production. Activity-based protein profiling revealed PqsC, an intracellular enzyme involved in Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) quorum sensing, as the primary molecular target. Accordingly, global proteomic analysis revealed widespread dysregulation of enzymes associated with the pyocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Biochemical assays confirmed inhibition of recombinant PqsBC, while intact protein mass spectrometry and site-directed mutagenesis established active site Cys129 as the covalent binding site. X-ray crystallography of the inhibited complex revealed a covalent binding mode. Subsequent virtual screening identified a chloroacetamide scaffold that exhibited enhanced potency and a well-defined binding mode. Importantly, supernatants from treated bacterial cultures showed reduced cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells, consistent with attenuated virulence. Collectively, this study identifies novel covalent inhibitors of PqsC and provides a mechanistic framework for the development of pathoblockers against P. aeruginosa.

item.title: Coupling Ligand Tuning With Polymer‐Induced Aperture Regulation for Molecular Sieving in Flexible MOFs
item.description:
Ligand pre-tuning coupled with polymer-induced aperture regulation enables CO2/N2 molecular sieving in flexible ZIF fillers. PEGDA partially occupies ZIF pores and restricts framework dynamics in XLPEGDA MMMs, enhancing diffusion-based molecular discrimination. Extension to ZIF-7 and ZIF-67 demonstrates the broader applicability of polymer-induced transport regulation across flexible MOFs.


ABSTRACT

Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO2/N2 size-sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF-8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO2/N2 molecular sieve. During mixed-matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid-state NMR (1H-13C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO2/N2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF-8-NH2 with 6 mol% 2-aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer-free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO2/N2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO2/N2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF-7 and ZIF-67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

item.title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
item.description:
HOMO-level alignment, not electron density, governs charge-transfer efficiency in donor–acceptor COF iodine hosts. This descriptor enables chemisorptive iodine anchoring, suppresses polyiodide dissolution, and accelerates charge transfer. The optimally designed NT-COF combines a triphenylamine donor with a naphthalene diimide acceptor, achieving high iodine loading with stable cycling and reliable low-temperature operation.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade-off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor–acceptor (D–A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge-transfer efficiency—with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. In this study, we establish highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level alignment relative to iodine's redox potential as the governing descriptor for charge-transfer efficiency. Analyzing a series of units with progressively elevated HOMO levels reveals a clear trend: higher HOMO levels enhance electron donation to iodine and promote charge transfer. The optimally designed NT-COF, which combines a triphenylamine (TPA) donor with favorable HOMO alignment and a naphthalene diimide (NTCDI) acceptor with extended conjugation, exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Even with a high iodine loading (∼50.5 wt%), it delivers stable cycling and reliable low-temperature operation. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the energetic alignment facilitates chemisorptive iodine anchoring, accelerates charge transfer, and suppresses polyiodide dissolution. This synergy confirms that rational COF design must combine energy-level alignment with structural conjugation.

item.title: Stabilizing Oxygen Redox in Polycrystalline Li‐Rich Layered Cathodes via Efficient Grain Boundary Passivation
item.description:
Polycrystalline Li-rich layered cathodes suffer from oxygen loss and grain-boundary degradation during cycling. Here, tannic-acid-assisted infiltration drives Ba to the outer surface and buried grain boundaries, where heat treatment converts it into an epitaxially coupled BaMO3− δ interphase. This ultrathin passivation layer suppresses oxygen release and interfacial side reactions, stabilizing oxygen redox and improving long-term cycling.


ABSTRACT

High-voltage cathodes with hybrid anion and cation redox activities, such as Li-rich and Mn-rich oxides, offer a pathway to higher energy density in lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). However, those cathodes suffer from oxygen loss from both the surface and grain boundaries, especially in traditional polycrystalline cathodes with secondary-particle morphology. Interfacial passivation is needed, yet uniform, high-quality coating at both primary- and secondary-particle levels remains challenging. Here, using a tannic acid-assisted process, we demonstrate an in situ formed BaMO3− δ (M = Ni, Co, and Mn) perovskite phase at surfaces and grain boundaries, offering effective passivation to suppress structural and electrochemical degradation. Differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS), soft X-ray spectroscopy (SXAS) and resonant inelastic X-ray spectroscopy (RIXS) reveal that the passivated grain boundaries effectively mitigate oxygen release, promote the retention of oxidized oxygen within the grains, and improve oxygen-redox reversibility. The stabilization is facilitated by strong M─O bonding at primary-particle surfaces, improving energy-density stability and mitigating voltage decay. The improved electrochemical performance results from the reliable coating method, which constructs sequential interfacial bonding along grain boundaries. Using earth-abundant elements only, this process may offer high-quality passivation for a variety of oxide cathodes used in LIBs and beyond.

item.title: Zinc–Halide–Integrated Thermally Reprocessable Molecular–Emitter Supramolecular Glass Scintillators for High–Resolution X–Ray Imaging
item.description:
We reported an effective strategy for the high−performance re−processable phosphorescent supramolecular glasses scintillators by employing a facile melt−quenching method. The optimized TNP−ZnI2 glass achieved a system spatial resolution of 28.4 lp mm−1 for high−fidelity x−ray imaging and reconstructed 3D x−ray imaging. After 10 fragment−soften−recast cycles, it retained 84% of its initial radioluminescence intensity while preserving the emission maximum and spectral profile. This work establishes a modular strategy for supramolecular−glass scintillators in which molecular emission and heavy−atom functionality are partitioned between complementary ionic components.


ABSTRACT

Transparent glass scintillators suppress grain−boundary scattering, but in many metal−halide glasses x−ray attenuation and terminal emission originate from the same local coordination unit, making their optimization mutually constraining. Here, we report molecular−emitter supramolecular glasses that functionally partition these roles between an organic phosphonium chromophore and a stoichiometrically incorporated zinc–halide environment. The phosphonium salt melt quenching methyl(4−(diphenylamino)phenyl)diphenylphosphonium iodide (o-TNP) with ZnX2 (X = Cl, Br, or I) and a trace amount of 4,4′−bipyridine (BP) produced transparent amorphous materials with glass−transition temperatures above 100°C. Across the halide series, the principal emission maximum remained within 493–500 nm, whereas the photoluminescence quantum yield increased from 3.53% to 10.01%, the average long−lived emission lifetime decreased from 9.7 to 4.4 µs, and the attenuation−corrected light yield rose from 14 909 to 22 954 photons MeV−1. The optimized TNP−ZnI2 screen achieved a system spatial resolution of 28.4 lp mm−1 at a thickness of 650 µm. After ten fragment−soften−recast cycles at 220°C, it retained 84% of its initial radioluminescence while preserving the emission maximum and spectral profile. This work provides a modular route for functional partitioning x−ray attenuation and long-lived excited-state dynamics with minimal perturbation of terminal emission energy.

item.title: Rh0–Rhδ+ Synergy Enables Hydroxyl‐Directed Electrocatalytic Hydrogenation of Guaiacol
item.description:
Electronically asymmetric Rh0–Rhδ+ sites promote hydroxyl-directed dual-siteadsorption and localized polarization of the aromatic π system of guaiacol, thereby lowering the barrier for initial aromatic-ring hydrogenation and delivering a 22-fold higher 2-methoxycyclohexanol yield rate than that of Rh0–Rh0.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic hydrogenation (ECH) of lignin-derived guaiacol offers an appealing route toward sustainable chemical production but is impeded by the exceptional stability of aromatic rings. Conventional rhodium catalysts with electronically symmetric Rh0–Rh0 sites generally activate guaiacol through Rh0-arene π interactions. However, the induced electronic perturbation remains largely delocalized over the arene π system, resulting in only limited local polarization and sluggish dearomatizing hydrogenation kinetics. Here, we introduce a hydroxyl-directed activation strategy that exploits the phenolic hydroxyl group as an intrinsic handle for aromatic-ring activation. Spatially adjacent Rh0 and Rhδ+ sites (Rh0–Rhδ+) were constructed in RhOx clusters through lattice-oxygen-mediated electrochemical reconstruction. The electron-deficient Rhδ+ sites selectively anchor the phenolic hydroxyl group, perturbing resonance donation from the phenolic oxygen into the aromatic ring and inducing asymmetric redistribution of aromatic π-electron density. This hydroxyl-directed adsorption simultaneously orients the aromatic ring toward neighboring Rh0 sites, thereby promoting d→π* back-donation and lowering the hydrogenation barrier. The resultant Rh0–Rhδ+ catalyst achieves a 2-methoxycyclohexanol production rate of 197.51 mmol h−1 gRh −1, which is 22-fold higher than that of Rh0–Rh0. Our findings establish hydroxyl-directed aromatic-ring activation as an effective strategy for overcoming aromatic inertia, providing a design principle for the electrocatalytic upgrading of lignin-derived aromatics.

item.title: Operando Identification of the Active Phase in Sr‐Promoted Lanthanum Cobaltite Perovskite‐Derived Catalysts for Ammonia Decomposition
item.description:
Ammonia decomposition catalyzed by base metals: Exsolution of cobalt from perovskites prepared by spray-flame synthesis (SFS) yields highly active, SrO-promoted Co/La2O3 catalysts with low cobalt content. Operando studies provide insight into the function of the promoter. Dynamic surface reconstruction under operating conditions increases the interface between SrO and Co and prevents the blocking of active Co sites by mobile La-containing species.


ABSTRACT

Storing energy in molecular form, particularly hydrogen in carbon-free carriers such as ammonia, is considered a key strategy for future energy systems. The release of hydrogen via ammonia decomposition is a critical step in this context that requires scalable and economically viable catalysts. In this work, spray-flame synthesis (SFS) was employed to prepare La1– x Sr x CoO3− δ (0≤ x ≤ 1) nanoparticles (≈ 10 nm), which serve as precursors for SrO-promoted Co/La2O3 catalysts prepared by exsolution. ESR, operando XRD, and ambient pressure photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provide insights into dynamic interfacial restructuring of the catalysts under the harsh ammonia decomposition conditions. The catalysts contain 25 wt% Co and achieve a maximum hydrogen productivity of 108 mmolH2${\mathrm{mmo}}{{\mathrm{l}}_{{{\mathrm{H}}_{\mathrm{2}}}}}$·gCo −1·min−1 at 500°C for the La0.75Sr0.25CoO3− δ -derived material. The coverage of La2O3 with SrO/Sr─OH species under reaction conditions inhibits the migration of La-based species, which block active Co sites in the absence of the promoter. An excess of Sr, however, promotes the growth of Co particles and reduces the exposed Co surface area. Beyond its structural role, operando APXPS reveals that SrO also influences reaction kinetics by facilitating NHx decomposition and weakening the binding strength of nitrogen, which is consistent with an electrostatic effect of SrO.

item.title: Correction to “Activatable Semiconducting Polymer Pro‐Nanomodulators for Deep‐Tissue Sono‐Immunotherapy of Orthotopic Pancreatic Cancer”
item.description: Angewandte Chemie International Edition, EarlyView.

item.title: Decoupling OH and H Binding via Dual‐Site Conductive MOFs for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Herein, a series of M–Cu dual-metal-site catalysts with tunable d-electron configurations was constructed on a conductive MOF platform for efficient alkaline hydrogen evolution. The modulation of d-electron filling downshifts the d-band center and creates a volcano-shaped trend for water dissociation. The Co–Cu dual-metal sites at the apex enable optimal adsorption of hydroxyl and water to effectively promote the Volmer step.


ABSTRACT

Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high-performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d-electron modulation strategy on dual-metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well-defined Cu-based two-dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu-HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d-electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d-electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d-band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano-type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual-site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen-bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d-electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.

item.title: Inside Back Cover: LEGO‐Like Granular‐Electrode Capacitive Deionization with Ultrahigh Mass Loading for Ultrafast Electrochemical Ion Capture (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 44/2026)
item.description: By assembling carbon granular electrodes (GEs) into a building block-like architecture, membrane-free granular-electrode capacitive deionization achieves ultrahigh mass loading while preserving short ion-transport paths. Forced convection then drives the ion-entrainment effect, renewing ions in both the inter-GE space and accessible intra-GE domain. This improved ion transport mitigates concentration polarization and sustains rapid electrochemical ion capture under high areal flux. More in the Research Article e9170775, Fei Yu, Jie Ma, and co-workers.

item.title: Inside Front Cover: Step‐Associated Cu‐Ceria Interfaces Enhance Catalytic Activity and Selectivity (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 44/2026)
item.description: In the Research Article e5628406, Jeffrey T. Miller, Yong Wang, Weixin Huang, and co-workers report how the anchoring environment of Cu nanoparticles on CeO2 becomes a catalytic design variable. By localizing similarly sized Cu nanoparticles at surface steps rather than terraces, distinct Cu–CeO2 interfacial structures are created, facilitating formate conversion toward methanol. The work reveals that nanoparticle location can govern interfacial chemistry and, consequently, catalytic activity and selectivity.

item.title: Outside Front Cover: Adaptive Hydrogenation of Alkynes Using CO as a Molecular Trigger to Selectively Produce Alkanes or Z‐Alkenes (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 44/2026)
item.description: One Catalyst, Two Reactivities: CO makes the Switch and Enables Adaptivity. Supported palladium nanoparticles adapt to their environment to hydrogenate alkynes to alkanes under H2, and to Z-alkenes upon incorporation of CO. The CO-triggered selectivity switch is fully reversible, rapid, and robust, and enables adaptive hydrogenation of 37 structurally diverse alkynes to valuable bioactive and pharmaceutical intermediates. In the Research Article e9302519, Walter Leitner, Alexis Bordet, and co-workers. Artwork by Dr. Johannes Zenner.

item.title: Intermediate‐Mediated Selectivity in Electrocatalytic Nitrate Reduction for Nitrogen Product Synthesis
item.description:
Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction reaction (eNO3RR) offers a sustainable route for nitrate removal and nitrogen valorization, yet its selectivity is governed by complex intermediate evolution. This Review focuses on intermediate behaviors in eNO3RR, covering their transformation pathways, detection methods, and regulation strategies. By linking mechanistic insights with catalyst and interfacial design, it highlights opportunities to steer nitrate conversion toward NH3, N2, or NH2OH.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic nitrate (NO3 −) reduction reaction (eNO3RR) has emerged as a promising strategy for waste NO3 − valorization, offering opportunities for environmental remediation. However, its complex proton-coupled electron transfer processes involve multiple competing pathways, in which the fate of key intermediates governs reaction activity and product selectivity. In this review, we provide an intermediate-centered perspective on eNO3RR, covering the reaction pathways from NO3 − activation to the selective synthesis of NH3, N2, and NH2OH. We then summarize current techniques for probing N-containing intermediates and active hydrogen (*H). On this basis, we discuss how catalyst design and microenvironment engineering regulate key processes in eNO3RR, including intermediate adsorption, retention and desorption, N─O bond cleavage, hydrogenation, and N─N coupling. We also examine the emerging role of data-driven approaches in optimizing eNO3RR systems. Drawing these discussions together, we distill principles for selective product synthesis. Finally, we discuss remaining challenges in achieving a deeper mechanistic understanding, regulating the interfacial microenvironment, and applying eNO3RR to real wastewater.

item.title: The Strategies of Improving Chemical Stability of Imine‐Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description:
Chemical stability is one of the crucial features for the practical applications of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). This review summarizes the important advances in improving the stability of imine-linked COFs from the viewpoint of design strategies, including electron-donating group substitution, fluorine substitution, redox conversion, six-membered cyclization, five-membered cyclization, and so on. An outlook of the challenges and future opportunities of these strategies is described to promote the realization of stable imine-linked COFs.


ABSTRACT

Imine-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have wide applications in molecular separation, gas storage, photocatalysis, electrocatalysis, energy storage, and optoelectronic devices because of their unique advantages such as good crystallinity, permanent porosity, and tunable pore structure. However, the practical applications of imine-linked COFs in chemical catalysis and gas separation may be hindered due to their reduced chemical stability in acidic or basic conditions. Recently, various effective strategies have been developed to improve chemical stability of imine-linked COFs. In this review, we summarize the important advances in improving the stability of imine-linked COFs from the viewpoint of design strategies, including electron-donating group substitution, steric tuning, fluorine substitution, redox conversion, six-membered cyclization, five-membered cyclization, and so on. Moreover, the challenges and perspectives are also described to promote the realization of stable imine-linked COFs, which will meet the requirements of these materials in practical applications.

item.title: Reusable Polyphenol Building Blocks Enable Recyclable Epoxy‐Amine Thermosets via Methanolysis
item.description:
A biobased epoxy–amine platform was developed using functional building blocks derived from polyphenols. These thermosets exhibited tunable mechanical and thermal properties, together with efficient, catalyst-free chemical recycling via methanolysis. Beyond the recovery of reusable building blocks, the recycled polyols could be further upcycled into antibacterial materials. This work provides guiding principles for the design of structurally tunable and recyclable epoxy–amine thermosets.


ABSTRACT

Biobased polyphenols represent attractive alternatives to bisphenol A for epoxy thermosets, yet most bio-derived epoxy networks remain permanently cross-linked and are difficult to recycle. Herein, we report a modular molecular design strategy that converts renewable polyphenols into reusable functional building blocks for recyclable epoxy–amine thermosets. Distinct from conventional degradable epoxy networks, this platform enables systematic structural variation and establishes a clear structure–depolymerization relationship. Kinetic and computational analyses further support a previously unrecognized ether-assisted methanolysis mechanism, in which neighboring ether functionalities and a favorable aliphatic amine environment lower the apparent kinetic barrier and modulate the local methanol environment around the cleavable ester bonds in a configuration-dependent manner. Consequently, the resulting thermosets undergo efficient methanolysis under mild conditions (70°C), affording reusable molecular components while maintaining tunable thermal and mechanical properties. Furthermore, carbon fiber–reinforced composites based on the optimized formulation can be efficiently depolymerized, yielding intact fibers and reusable building blocks in 88% isolated yield. The recovered polyols can be further upcycled into antibacterial quaternary ammonium materials, demonstrating a value-added reuse pathway. This work identifies a previously unrecognized molecular promotion mechanism for catalyst-free methanolysis and translates this mechanism insight into a structural design principle for recyclable polyphenol-based epoxy–amine thermosets.

item.title: Speed Control of Single Molecules on a Surface
item.description:
The speed of a single molecule moving across a silver crystal surface is determined with the tip of a scanning tunneling microscope (STM). Travelling distances Δx and travelling times Δt, which are determined simultaneously with high precision, allow to directly measure time–distance relationships. It turns out that atomic defects in the surface strongly affect the travelling time with very high sensitivity to their precise location.


ABSTRACT

Laws of motion are of fundamental importance for the understanding of dynamic systems. At the atomic scale, the kinetic energy of molecules controls chemical reactions. The velocity of individual molecules, however, has never been measured, because it is difficult to determine time–distance relationships. Here, we show how the real speed of a single molecule moving across a Ag(111) surface is measured at the microsecond time scale. We found that atomic defects extend the travelling time by orders of magnitude, even at distances of few nanometers from the molecule and with high sensitivity to their precise location. Statistical measurements, obtained by repetitive translation of a single molecule in an oscillating electric field, give insight into the time scales of molecular motion in a confined environment. The strong influence of the defects underscores the need for their investigation during chemical reactions or collision experiments at variable velocities and geometries on a surface.

item.title: To Dope Mo3+ in Colloidal Nanocrystals
item.description:
Colloidal Mo3+-doped Cs2AgInCl6 double perovskite nanocrystals (∼9 nm), and their thin films are prepared. The samples show narrow NIR-II emission around 1105 nm, because of intra-configurational spin-flip d-d transition of Mo3+. Our nanocrystal synthesis enables solution-phase and thin film-based optoelectronics of Mo3+ NIR-II emission.


ABSTRACT

Mo3+ shows intra-configurational spin-flip (ICSF) d → d electronic transitions, emitting near-infrared-II (NIR-II) radiation. Till date, the emission has been reported from Mo3+-doped into bulk host materials, in the powder or single crystalline forms. Here we report the synthesis of Mo3+ doping in a colloidal nanocrystal (NC). Colloidal Mo3+-doped Cs2AgInCl6 double perovskite NCs are prepared using a typical hot-injection method in a non-polar medium. The challenges of poor solubility of molybdenum precursor and instability of low oxidation state of Mo3+ in the reaction medium are overcome by a rational design of the synthesis. The resulting NCs have cubic shape with edge length ∼9 nm, and oleylammonium ions as the predominant surface capping ligands. The colloidal synthesis enabled us to fabricate thin films of Mo3+-doped NCs by spin-coating technique. Both colloidal NCs and their films show the sharp Mo3+ ICSF NIR-II emission around 1105 nm. Temperature dependent (7-300 K) PL spectra and lifetime studies provide mechanistic insights about the spin- and Laporte-selection rules of the ICSF emission from [MoCl6]3− octahedral unit. This report of a colloidal NC with Mo3+ dopants, and their thin films, is expected to open up research avenues for micro-LEDs and quantum light emitters in NIR-II region.

item.title: Luminescence Vapochromism of a Cu(I)/Na Phosphane Iodide Assembly Based on a Secondary‐Sphere Sodium Response
item.description:
The luminescence of a heterometallic d-s {Cu2I2Na2} phosphane-phosphinate aggregate is regulated by an interplay of Na+–π/I– contacts and reversible coordination of oxygen-containing organic molecules to Na ions. Structural variations caused by the incoming guest lead to a wide and selective variation of the emission color and illustrate a new approach to responsive metal complexes constructed from soft-hard donor ligands.


ABSTRACT

Photoluminescent compounds showing distinct and selective optical response to external perturbation are essential components for sensing applications. Herein, we present a copper(I) iodide–sodium luminescent complex assembled with a hybrid phosphane-phosphinate ligand. The photoemission of the tetrametallic {Cu2I2Na2} aggregate is consistent with the thermally activated delayed fluorescence that originates from the [CuI(phosphane)] motifs but strongly depends on the coordination environment of sodium ions completed by O-donor solvent molecules, Na–π(phenyl) interactions, and/or Na–I bonds. The reversible removal and vapor-phase addition of methanol, ethanol, water, and dimethoxyethane as Na-bound ligands alter the solid-state luminescence from blue (461 nm) to yellow (570 nm) with quantum yields reaching 0.73. Importantly, different photoemission responses to methanol (522 nm) and ethanol (492 nm) are complemented by preferred binding of methanol and its detection in up to 1:10 methanol:ethanol mixtures. Variations of luminescence among the studied solvates are attributed to the alterations of secondary sphere interactions involving sodium ions and illustrate a new approach to stimuli-responsive metal complexes constructed from soft-hard donor ligands.

item.title: A Mechanical sp2‐Jail for C60 Fullerene
item.description:
A rigid bisporphyrin receptor with an exceptionally compact 3D cavity functions as a molecular “mechanical jail”, tightly enclosing C60 fullerene. Near-perfect shape complementarity affords ultrahigh binding affinity while imposing a large kinetic barrier for guest exchange, rendering encapsulation effectively irreversible under ambient conditions.


ABSTRACT

Being an iconic spherical molecule exclusively composed of sp 2 carbon atoms, the development of increasingly efficient synthetic receptors for C60 fullerene remains a pressing challenge in supramolecular chemistry. However, as tighter hosts that employ most of their cavity volumes to complementarily encapsulate C60 are developed, steric constraints may emerge that mechanically trap this ball-shaped guest within their lumen. Here we explore this unprecedented scenario with a rigid bisporphyrin sp2 -receptor that acts as a “mechanical jail” for C60. This exceptional host presents the tightest 3D cavity reported for this spherical guest, occupying 77% of the internal volume and enabling strong π–π and CH⋯π interactions, which result in exceptionally high binding affinities (Ka  > 109 M− 1). Unlike related cage and basket analogues, encapsulation in this perfectly fitted host is kinetically hindered, leading to guest release dynamics that are extremely slow above 400 K and essentially suppressed at room temperature.

item.title: Deuterated Multi‐Color Probes for Reaction‐Resolved Mapping of Intracellular Redox Pathways With Magnetic Resonance
item.description:
Reaction-dependent conversion of sp2-D to sp3-D encodes intracellular redox processes as distinct 2H NMR signals. A single deuterated probe simultaneously reports glutathione conjugation and enzymatic reduction, providing a pathway-resolved magnetic resonance readout in living cells.


ABSTRACT

Deuterium (2H) offers unique advantages as a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) reporter owing to its negligible endogenous biological background and ability to provide chemically distinguishable resonances. In the present study, we propose a chemical-shift encoding concept in which reactions converting the deuterium-bearing carbon from an sp2- to an sp3-hybridized state produce pronounced and predictable 2H NMR chemical-shift changes, enabling distinct reaction outcomes to be encoded as spectroscopically resolvable signatures. Here we introduce deuterated “multi-color” probes (DMCPs), a molecular platform coupling reaction-based molecular recognition with 2H NMR spectroscopy to simultaneously map distinct intracellular redox pathways. DMCPs encode thiol conjugation and enzymatic reduction as spectrally separable 2H NMR signatures, allowing multiplexed detection of glutathione reactivity and NAD(P)H-driven reductive activity within a single acquisition. Applied in living glioblastoma cells, DMCPs reveal parallel glutathione conjugation and NAD(P)H-dependent reduction, with the corresponding reaction-derived signals changing upon glutathione depletion. This method further captures pharmacologically induced redox perturbations, providing a mechanistic framework for evaluating redox-targeting strategies and rationalizing resistance mechanisms in early-stage drug discovery.

item.title: Sulfur‐Boron Lewis Pair‐Catalyzed Hydrohalogenation of Alkynes via Formal Hydrogen Atom Transfer
item.description:
A sulfur-boron Lewis pair enables the stereodivergent hydrohalogenation of alkynes with exclusive Markovnikov selectivity. Mechanistic studies support a proton transfer-electron transfer (PT-ET) sequence for vinyl radical formation rather than a concerted hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) pathway.


ABSTRACT

The catalytic synthesis of both (E)- and (Z)-haloalkenes from internal aryl alkyl alkynes via a sulfur-boron Lewis pair has been developed. The catalytically active Lewis pair complex is generated in situ from 2-naphthalenethiol and B(C6F5)3, enabling the selective synthesis of chloro-, bromo-, and iodoalkenes with exclusive Markovnikov regioselectivity. Both (E)- and (Z)-haloalkenes were obtained in good yields with high selectivities by simply controlling the reaction temperature. Experimental mechanistic studies support the intermediacy of vinyl radicals generated through an overall formal hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) process. Computational investigations further support a stepwise proton transfer-electron transfer (PT-ET) mechanism rather than a concerted HAT event. The origin of the stereodivergence is also elucidated by combining experimental observations with theoretical calculations. This work demonstrates a new strategy for vinyl radical generation through sulfur-boron Lewis pair catalysis and suggests that formal HAT reactivity can emerge from a stepwise PT-ET mechanism in main-group catalysis.

item.title: One‐Pot Synthesis of Aqueous PEDOT‐Based Conductive Inks via Sequential RAFT/Oxidative Polymerization
item.description:
We developed a fast, aqueous one-pot synthesis for PEDOT:PSTFSI, combining sequential reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) and oxidative polymerization. This method eliminates toxic solvents and purification steps, achieving full monomer conversion in under 3 h. The resulting dispersions form conductive films (up to 120 S cm−1) and align with six green chemistry principles, enabling sustainable, scalable organic electronics.


ABSTRACT

The rising demand for flexible and printable electronics has driven significant interest in π-conjugated polymers, in particular for poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT), which is traditionally stabilized by poly(styrenesulfonate) (PSS). In the recent years, our group has been investigating poly[4-styrenesulfonyl(trifluoromethylsulfonyl)imide] (PSTFSI) as a promising alternative polyelectrolyte, yielding PEDOT:PSTFSI dispersions with enhanced ionic conductivity, reduced acidity, and lower hygroscopicity. Although this polymer complex offers great potential in organic electronics, its synthesis still requires long reactions times (up to several days) and the use of toxic organic solvents with tedious intermediate purification steps, limiting its scalability and sustainability. Herein, we report an innovative aqueous one-pot synthesis of PEDOT:PSTFSI dispersion, by combining reversible addition–fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) and oxidative polymerization in an aqueous one-pot process. This approach eliminates the need for harmful solvents and intermediate purifications, achieving full monomer conversion in less than 4 h and excellent control over macromolecular structure of PSTFSI (30–300 kg mol−1 with Đ often below 1.1). Following the one-pot oxidative polymerization, the resulting PEDOT:PSTFSI dispersions exhibit filamentous network morphologies, forming highly percolated conductive films upon printing, with charge conductivities up to 120 S cm−1.

item.title: Breaking the Diffusion–Dispersion Trade‐Off: Subnanometric MoO3 Clusters in Interzeolite Transformation Intermediates for Oxidative Desulfurization With H2O2
item.description:
A protozeolite-mediated defect engineering strategy is proposed for stabilizing ∼1.27 nm MoO3 clusters within an interzeolite transformation intermediate matrix. This rationally designed catalyst couples a sterically unhindered porous network with a highly reactive silanol microenvironment, enabling the unrestricted deep oxidation of bulky molecules.


ABSTRACT

Overcoming the intractable trade-off between restricted bulky molecule diffusion in microporous zeolites and poor active-metal dispersion on mesoporous supports remains a formidable challenge, particularly in the deep oxidative desulfurization of fuel oils. Herein, by strategically trapping metastable amorphous protozeolites during the interzeolite transformation of FAU to Beta zeolite, we engineered a Mo-functionalized interzeolite transformation intermediate (Mo-AZ) featuring abundant silanol defects and a well-established mesoporous architecture. These silanols serve as robust anchoring sites, yielding a unique (Si─O─)1Mo(─O─Mo)5 interfacial coordination that firmly stabilizes MoO3 species as sub-nanometric clusters (∼1.27 nm). Crucially, the hierarchical mesoporous network eradicates the spatial steric hindrance for bulky sulfur substrates, while the highly hydrophilic silanol microenvironment not only specifically enriches the oxidant of hydrogen peroxide but dynamically promotes its spontaneous cleavage into ultra-reactive superoxide radicals. Consequently, Mo-AZ exhibits exceptional catalytic activity and robust structural stability for deep oxidative desulfurization. This work decisively dismantles the mass-transfer barriers in the catalytic conversion of bulky molecules, pioneering a novel paradigm for designing high-performance sub-nanocluster catalysts via the defect engineering of metastable protozeolites.

item.title: Photochromic Hybrid Organic‐Inorganic Metal Halide Glasses
item.description:
Vitrification transforms the organic–inorganic metal halide 4-MeOBPP2ZnBr4 (4-MeOBPP+ = 4-methoxybenzyltriphenylphosphonium) into a glass whose medium-range disorder creates photoactive motifs absent from the crystal. In g-4-MeOBPP2ZnBr4, these motifs promote intermolecular charge separation, activating sub-second UV photochromism and pronounced x-ray-induced photochromism, and revealing a glass-enabled route to turn-on optical responses.


ABSTRACT

Melt-quenching provides an effective route to glass formation while reconfiguring the atomic and electronic structures of materials. Despite the accompanying changes in mechanical and optical properties, how the resulting disorder can be exploited to enable functionalities beyond those of crystalline phases remains insufficiently understood. Here, we show that a hybrid organic-inorganic metal halide (OIMH) glass, g-4-MeOBPP2ZnBr4 (4-MeOBPP+ = 4-methoxybenzyltriphenylphosphonium), exploits vitrification-induced disorder to deliver a sub-second UV-triggered photochromic response absent in its crystalline counterpart, together with pronounced x-ray-induced photochromism. Upon UV irradiation, the initially colorless glass rapidly turns red, reaching 50% of the saturation absorbance within 0.5 s. Reverse Monte Carlo modeling combined with time-dependent density functional theory indicates that medium-range structural disorder generates locally perturbed environments that can serve as photoactive motifs. These motifs can host energetically proximate singlet and triplet states (ΔE ST ∼ 0.02 eV), favoring intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge separation between adjacent cations. Guided by this design rationale, two glass analogs, g-4-MeOBPP2CdBr4 and g-3-MeOBPP2ZnBr4 (3-MeOBPP+ = 3-methoxybenzyltriphenylphosphonium cation), are also found to exhibit vitrification-induced photochromism. These findings identify medium-range disorder as an effective design lever in OIMH molecular glasses, providing a conceptual framework for creating turn-on optical responses in disordered materials.

item.title: Site‐Specific Functioning of CuN3–PdS3 Janus Dual‐Atom Sites Enable Near‐Unity Faradaic Efficiency for Nitrate Electroreduction to Ammonia
item.description:
A Janus CuN3–PdS3 dual-atom catalyst on N/S co-doped carbon (CuPd-SNC) spatially decouples nitrate adsorption/activation from hydrogen supply during electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR). The Cu sites activate NOx intermediates, Pd sites provide reactive hydrogen, and N/S bridges mediate *H spillover, enabling 99.58% Faradaic efficiency for ammonia synthesis and stable Zn–nitrate battery operation.


ABSTRACT

Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) using renewable electricity offers a carbon-free and energy-saving route to remediating nitrate-polluted wastewater while producing ammonia (NH3). However, conventional catalysts for NO3RR suffer from strong adsorption of NOx intermediates that hinders further hydrogenation, resulting in diminished selectivity and catalyst deactivation. Here we construct a Janus-type CuN3−PdS3 dual-atom catalyst featuring N/S dual bridging, namely CuPd-SNC, to enable decoupled NOx species adsorption and hydrogen supply for hydrogenation on Cu and Pd sites, respectively. Excitingly, CuPd-SNC delivers a near-unity Faradaic efficiency of 99.58% for NH3 synthesis and a production rate of 1.34 mmol h−1 cm−2. When integrated into a Zn–nitrate battery, CuPd-SNC achieves a maximum power density of 13.0 mW cm−2 and demonstrates stable operation for >160 h. In situ spectroscopic and theoretical analyses reveal the site-specific functionalities of the CuN3−PdS3 Janus configuration, wherein Cu sites markedly enhance the adsorption/activation of NOx − intermediates, Pd sites enable continuous proton supply and reduce the energy barriers for multi-step *NOx hydrogenation, while N/S dual bridges serve as a proton reservoir. These findings highlight the site-specific but complementary functioning of dual-atom catalysts in synergistically pushing the limit of conventional electrocatalysts, offering fundamental insights into the rational catalyst design for NH3 synthesis.

item.title: Loose Al3+ Solvation Aggregates Enable Reversible Aluminum Anodes in Chlorine‐Free Electrolyte
item.description:
Loose solvation aggregates (LAGs), enabled by TPFPB-assisted solvation regulation, facilitate rapid ion transport and suppress excessive interfacial passivation. The resulting stable hybrid interphase enables reversible Al metal anode in chlorine-free electrolytes.


ABSTRACT

Sustained reversible Aluminum plating/stripping with long cycle life is scarcely realized in chlorine-free organic electrolytes. The electrolyte formula exerts the deposition/stripping behavior of metal anodes. Highly polarizing Al3+ cations show strong binding with electrolyte components, resulting in a significantly different ionic solvation structure from lithium. Here we reveal that pervasive compact ion aggregates (CAGs) solvation structures with an Al3+–Al3+ interatomic distance of ∼5 Å were formed within typical ether or ester electrolytes, leading to low ionic conductivity and passivation interphases. On this basis, we developed a chlorine-free ester electrolyte featuring loose solvation aggregates (LAGs) with an Al3+–Al3+ interatomic distance of 7 Å through modulating the balance of Al3+ coordination between the OTf− anion and solvent. Tris(pentafluorophenyl)borane (TPFPB) interacts with anions to suppress anion over-coordination in Al3+ solvation structures, thereby inducing an organic–inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This loosely solvated Al3+ electrolyte delivers nearly twofold enhanced ionic conductivity and a hybrid SEI, which endows the system with a low Al-plating/stripping overpotential of ∼0.4 V and durable cycling exceeding 4000 h.

item.title: BrIS: Visualizing Internal Standards at the MS1 Level via Bromine Fingerprint for Sensitive and Robust Proteomics Quality Control
item.description:
Brominated Internal Standards (BrIS) exhibit a distinctive bromine isotopic fingerprint that enables direct visualization at the MS1 level without requiring MS/MS spectra. Combined with BrScan-MS1, BrIS provides reliable retention-time assignment and consistent quantitative measurements for quality monitoring across diverse proteomic settings ranging from complex biological matrices to ultra-low-input single-cell samples.


ABSTRACT

Data fidelity in mass spectrometry (MS)-based proteomics demands stringent quality control, for which spiking internal standards into biological samples is a straightforward practice. Yet, conventional internal-standard tracking relies on MS/MS-dependent identification, which can be unavailable or unreliable under challenging analytical conditions. Herein, we introduce a suite of Brominated Internal Standards (BrIS) and a tailored scanning algorithm, BrScan-MS1, which exploits bromine isotopic fingerprints and conserved elution order of BrIS peptides to directly track them at the MS1 level and enable reliable retention time (RT) assignment. Across a DDA dilution series, BrScan-MS1 recognized all BrIS peptides in every BrIS-spiked replicate and provided consistent RT assignments. In long-term DIA analyses using a plasma matrix, BrIS showed greater RT stability and quantitative consistency than iRT peptides and enabled sensitive tracking of instrumental drift. Cross-platform analyses demonstrated robust BrIS-based RT calibration of endogenous peptides across LC-MS platforms. In single-cell proteomics involving three cell lines, BrIS enabled reliable tracking at low sample inputs while largely maintaining cell-line-specific proteomic patterns and showed a modest tendency to better preserve control-derived differential-expression patterns than iRT peptides. Together, BrIS and BrScan-MS1 provide a practical approach for quality control across diverse proteomics settings ranging from complex matrices to ultra-low-input samples.

item.title: Two‐Dimensional fes‐Topology Covalent Organic Frameworks With Intrinsic Paramagnetic Semiconducting Properties
item.description:
A series of two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks with fes-topology is constructed by tessellating octagonal and rhombic pores using distorted porphyrin building blocks. The orthogonal arrangement of redox-active units endows these frameworks with high electrical conductivity and electron mobility. Notably, the incorporation of tetrathiafulvalene generates stable radicals, imparting a strong paramagnetic response. This work demonstrates a modular strategy to integrate semiconducting and magnetic functionalities in 2D COFs, opening avenues for spintronic applications.


ABSTRACT

The structural diversity and periodic arrangement of two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) endow them with great promise for electronic and magnetic functionalities. Nevertheless, magnetic functionalities in semiconducting 2D COFs are not easily attainable due to the scarcity of effective topology diagrams and building blocks. In this study, we designed and synthesized three examples of fes-topology COFs by rationally tessellating octagonal and rhombic pores using redox-active building blocks. The resulting fes-net COFs exhibit high crystallinity, excellent porosity, and well-resolved pore structures. Furthermore, the highly ordered orthogonal arrangement of the embedded redox-active units endows these fes-net COFs with electrical conductivities up to 10−2 S cm−1. In particular, Cu-BBFPP-TQTA-COF displayed enhanced paramagnetic properties attributed to the generated stable tetrathiafulvalene radical species. This work provides an effective design strategy for constructing octagonal fes-COFs and offers new insights into the development of semiconducting magnets.

item.title: Anion Coordination Field Enables Ni/Mn Spin‐Orbital Reconstruction for Stable High‐Voltage Sodium Layer‐Structured Cathodes
item.description:
Mild nitrogen (N) coordination reshapes the local TM-(O,N) environment in an O3-type Na layered cathode, strengthening p-d covalency and crystal-field splitting while driving Ni-to-Mn charge redistribution. This electronic-structure modulation suppresses local distortion, stabilizes oxygen redox, and enables durable high-voltage cycling.


ABSTRACT

Ni/Mn-based O3-typed layer-structured oxides are attractive for high-voltage cathodes toward sodium batteries; however, the deep-desodiation stability is constrained by transition-metal orbital instability and localized oxygen redox. The anion-coordination local-electronic network was thus reconstructed in single-crystalline Na[Ni0.3Mn0.5Cu0.1Ti0.1]O2 through a polyvinylpyrrolidone-assisted mild nitridation strategy. The resulting Ni-N-Mn coordination can enhance Ni/Mn 3d-N 2p orbital coupling, driving Ni-to-Mn charge redistribution and stabilizing the low-spin Mn3+-like states by increasing local crystal-field splitting. This coordination-induced spin/orbital reconstruction can further generate an extended TM-(O,N)-TM p-d charge network that disperses high-voltage ligand holes and stabilizes lattice oxygen. The modified cathode delivers reduced polarization, improved Na+-transport kinetics, and a durable cycling lifespan at high voltage, with 91% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 2 C coupled with hard carbon. These findings demonstrate anion-coordination reconstruction as a direct route to regulating orbital occupation and oxygen redox in high-voltage layer-structured cathodes.

item.title: Redirecting Regioselectivity in Cytochrome P450 ApPT for B‐Ring Functionalization of Pentacyclic Triterpenoids
item.description:
A semi-rationally engineered P450 disrupts the native radical transfer pathway to achieve highly selective B-ring C7β functionalization of pentacyclic triterpenoids. The installed C7β-OH handle supports chemoenzymatic synthesis of previously inaccessible B-ring-modified PT derivatives with potent antitumor activity, demonstrating the utility of enzyme engineering for the late-stage diversification of complex natural products.


ABSTRACT

Pentacyclic triterpenoids (PTs) feature a steroid-like privileged scaffold, but late‑stage functionalization of their inert B‑ring C(sp3)─H bonds remains a formidable synthetic challenge due to the absence of directing groups and the consequent poor regio- and stereoselectivity. Here we report a semi-rationally engineered P450 variant, MB4, that enables highly selective C7β hydroxylation of 18β-glycyrrhetinic acid, achieving C–H activation on the B-ring with > 99% regioselectivity. Protein crystallography and computational studies revealed that the reshaped active pocket of MB4 disrupts the native 1,5-hydrogen atom transfer (1,5-HAT) relay oxidation, thereby redirecting the regioselectivity exclusively to the B-ring C7 position. The synthetic utility of MB4 was demonstrated through substrate scope investigation, large-scale preparation, and a chemoenzymatic synthesis platform that generated a library of previously inaccessible B-ring-modified PT derivatives. Biological evaluation showed that several C7-acylated derivatives exhibited antiproliferative activity (IC50 = 0.31–5.04 µM) by triggering caspase-3-dependent apoptosis and inducing G2/M-phase arrest. This work provides a promising blueprint for reprogramming P450 selectivity for late-stage C–H functionalization of polycyclic natural products.

item.title: Direct Access to Chiral Piperidines by Enantioselective HAT‐Initiated C(sp3)─H Oxidation
item.description:
The direct desymmetrization of piperidines is achieved through manganese-catalyzed enantioselective α-C(sp3 )─H oxidation with hydrogen peroxide, affording versatile chiral N,O-acetals in good yields and with high enantio- and diastereoselectivity. These intermediates provide access to diverse functionalized piperidines with retention of chirality.


ABSTRACT

Enantioselective C(sp3 )─H functionalization reactions are appealing synthetic organic chemistry tools to streamline access to valuable chiral molecules from simple precursors. Chiral piperidines are ubiquitous motifs in pharmaceuticals and natural products, yet methods for their preparation from simple non-chiral precursors remain limited. We report a catalytic strategy for the preparation of chiral piperidines by α-C(sp3 )─H oxidation of achiral piperidines using hydrogen peroxide as oxidant and an evolved manganese catalyst in 2,2,2-trifluoroethanol. Piperidines are desymmetrized to afford chemically versatile chiral N,O-acetal products in good yields, with high enantio- and diastereoselectivity. The resulting products serve as key intermediates to access a diverse range of functionalized piperidines while retaining chirality. Mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction proceeds via a highly enantioselective hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) followed by an electron transfer to generate a chiral iminium cation that is rapidly hydroxylated. Statistical models correlating reaction performance to molecular features provide a mechanistic basis for the stereoselective dictating elements and offer a tool for future reaction development.

item.title: Late‐Stage Annulative Imidazolation for Expanding Histidine‐Analogous Side Chains in Peptides and Proteins
item.description:
Re-engineering the classic Debus–Radziszewski reaction enables highly chemoselective, multicomponent N-imidazolation of complex peptides under mild aqueous conditions, providing a programmable platform for tuning peptide electrostatics, function, and structural diversity. Mechanistic studies revealed that the critical hydroxyl-elimination step of hydroimidazole precursors proceeds through distinct pathways under acidic versus basic conditions.


ABSTRACT

Histidine (His) plays indispensable roles in peptides and proteins owing to the unique reactivity and ionization properties of its imidazole side chain. However, the chemical space of imidazole-containing side chains remains remarkably underexplored, largely due to the synthetic challenges associated with the selective installation and diversification of imidazole motifs on complex biomolecules. Classical reactions for forming or modifying imidazoles typically require harsh conditions, limiting their applicability in sensitive biomolecular settings. Here, we report a mild and modular late-stage multi-component annulative imidazolation strategy for the direct installation of histidine-analogous side chains in peptides and proteins. In contrast to classical Debus–Radziszewski protocols, the reaction proceeds efficiently at ambient temperature under near-neutral to basic aqueous conditions, with water as the optimal cosolvent. The method enables rapid access to structurally diverse imidazole motifs with high chemoselectivity and biomolecular compatibility. Beyond providing facile access to noncanonical histidine analogues, this platform offers a programmable approach for tuning peptide electrostatics and function through late-stage side-chain modification.

item.title: Functional‐Group Synergy Regulates Dynamic Hydrogen‐Bond for High‐Rate and Wide‐Temperature Zinc Deep Eutectic Electrolytes
item.description:
Functional-group-regulated deep eutectic electrolyte (DEE), where NH2-enabled dynamic hydrogen-bond exchange transforms a rigid solvation network into an adaptive Zn2+ solvation structure, simultaneously accelerating ion transport, lowering desolvation barriers, and enabling robust interfacial chemistry for high-rate Zn batteries across −40°C to 60°C.


ABSTRACT

Zinc deep eutectic electrolytes (DEEs) have garnered increasing interest due to their unique physicochemical properties. However, simultaneously achieving high-rate capability and wide-temperature operation remains challenging because strong solvent–ion interactions increase both viscosity and desolvation barriers. Here, three model DEEs were constructed using propionamide, N-methylacetamide, and methylurea to systematically elucidate the roles of C═O, NH, and NH2 functional groups in regulating salt dissociation and hydrogen-bond networks. Comparative studies reveal that the cooperative C═O/NH groups govern efficient Zn-salt dissociation, whereas the additional NH2 group transforms a relatively rigid hydrogen-bond network into a dynamically reconfigurable one. The resulting enhanced dynamic hydrogen-bond exchange continuously reconstructs the Zn2+ solvation environment, lowers the desolvation barrier, increases ligand participation in the primary solvation sheath, and promotes the formation of a robust N/Cl-rich hybrid interphase. Consequently, the optimized ZCMI enables highly reversible Zn plating/stripping from −40°C to 60°C, sustains stable cycling for over 8000 h at −40°C, and supports current densities up to 10.0 mA·cm−2. Zn||PANI full cells exhibit excellent rate capability, retain 96% of their initial capacity after 1200 cycles at −40°C, and operate stably at 60°C. These findings establish dynamic hydrogen-bonding as a key descriptor governing solvation chemistry in zinc DEEs.

item.title: Interfacial OH− Dynamic Modulation by Alternating Current Enables Precipitation‐Suppressed Direct Seawater Electrolysis for Hydrogen Production
item.description:
Under AC, periodic polarity reversal enables one electrode to alternately function as cathode and anode, so that OH− from the hydrogen evolution reaction is promptly consumed by anodic OH−-consuming reaction on the same electrode, dynamically modulating interfacial OH− concentration to prevent local alkalization and precipitation, thereby achieving durable H2 production.


ABSTRACT

Direct seawater electrolysis (DSE) for H2 production suffers from severe performance degradation caused by the precipitation of Mg/Ca hydroxides, where OH− generated from the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) reacts with Mg2+/Ca2+ in seawater. To address this issue, we propose an innovative alternating current-driven DSE (AC-DSE) instead of conventional direct current-driven DSE (DC-DSE). Periodic polarity reversal under AC enables the same electrode to alternately function as cathode and anode, ensuring OH− from HER is promptly consumed by subsequent anodic OH−-consuming reaction. This dynamic interfacial OH− modulation prevents local alkalization and precipitation. Proof-of-concept experiments using PtRh electrodes validated that AC-DSE effectively prevents precipitation and maintains a stable current, in contrast to the rapid precipitation and performance decay observed in DC-DSE. FEM simulations and experimental established the optimal AC waveform and period for effective precipitation-suppressed and high Faradaic efficiency. Furthermore, by replacing the oxygen evolution reaction with ethylene glycol oxidation (EGOR), a reaction typically requiring strong alkali, the AC‑driven local microenvironment enables efficient HER‑EGOR coupling in neutral seawater. Importantly, this HER‑EGOR coupling system eliminates H2/O2 mixing risks, lowers energy consumption and co-produces value‑added chemicals. This work establishes AC-DSE as an effective and promising route for sustainable H2 production from seawater.

item.title: The Promise and Challenges of Ammonia Electrosynthesis From Dinitrogen and Water Using an Electrochemical Palladium Membrane
item.description:
Electrosynthesis of ammonia from nitrogen gas and water at ambient temperature is demonstrated using a device equipped with an electrochemical palladium membrane, which provides exclusive selectivity for the transfer of protons between the aqueous water oxidation and non-aqueous nitrogen reduction compartments. Fundamental and technical challenges associated with this approach are discussed.


ABSTRACT

Sustainable ammonia production can be achieved via an electrochemical process coupling the lithium redox-mediated nitrogen reduction (Li-NRR) with hydrogen oxidation, but a more practical approach uses water oxidation (the oxygen evolution reaction; OER) as the anode reaction. However, coupling the Li-NRR and the OER is restricted by incompatibility of the anhydrous conditions required for nitrogen reduction with water. Aiming to resolve this, we investigated an electrolyser with an electrochemical palladium-based membrane, which transforms protons generated by the OER to palladium hydride in aqueous media and releases protons into non-aqueous Li-NRR media to sustain ammonia production. The hydride formation/oxidation mechanism, validated through experiments with deuterated water, ensures exclusive membrane selectivity to protons, and is facilitated by the palladium-gold electrocatalysts. We demonstrate ammonia electrosynthesis from nitrogen (15 bar) and water at a faradaic efficiency of 59 ± 4%, yield rate of 20 ± 1 nmol s−1 cm−2 and energy efficiency of 9.0 ± 0.7% over more than two days. However, deeper investigation of the system revealed ammonia-promoted corrosion of the palladium-based membrane—a challenge that needs to be addressed in the future developments of this technology.

item.title: Spatially Decoupled Ion Transport and Mechanical Robustness Enabled by a Molecular Scaffold Strap in Gel Polymer Electrolytes
item.description:
A molecular scaffold strap strategy is introduced to regulate the gel polymer electrolytes. Size-matched ether molecules bridge adjacent polymer chains, creating a mechanically reinforced and homogeneous network while enabling structural Li+ transport through a fluorinated gradient solvation environment. This strategy decouples mechanical robustness from ion transport, enabling long lifespan and enhanced thermal safety in lithium metal batteries.


ABSTRACT

In situ gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs), which confine liquid electrolytes within a polymer matrix, are promising for realizing high-safety lithium (Li) metal batteries. However, the liquid phase and the polymer matrix act as reciprocal chokes: the liquid expedites ion transport but plasticizes the matrix and compromises its mechanical strength, whereas the matrix provides rigidity yet obstructs ionic conduction. In this study, we propose a molecular scaffold strap strategy that decouples the regulation of mechanical robustness and ion transport in GPEs. Specifically, six-arm monomers are employed to form a 3D polymer matrix, while ethylene glycol dibutyl ether, with a size-matched anchoring character, acts as a scaffold strap that strengthens adjacent polymer segments. Fluorinated carbonate cosolvents further facilitate Li+ transport and interfacial stability. The engineered GPE exhibits a high modulus of 8.9 MPa, ionic conductivity of 3.82 × 10−4 S cm−1, Li+ transference number of 0.68, and stable electrode interfaces. The Li||LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 pouch cell (2.7 Ah) achieves 87% capacity retention after 100 cycles and exhibits an elevated self-heating onset temperature of 160.7°C. Furthermore, a high energy density of 506 Wh kg−1 is demonstrated in the Cu||LiNi0.92Co0.03Mn0.05O2 pouch cell (3.5 Ah).

item.title: Overcoming Salt Precipitation in CO2 Reduction Membrane Electrode Assembly Electrolyzer Enables Over 4200 Hours Stable Operation
item.description:
Stable, precipitation-free CO2 electrolysis in membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) for over 4200 h enabled by integrating tetramethylammonium [(CH3)4N+] cations with continuous cation recovery.


ABSTRACT

Alkali metal cations (AMCs) are widely recognized as critical promoters of CO2 electroreduction. Yet, salt precipitation severely undermines membrane electrode assembly (MEA) electrolyzer stability, while limited mechanistic understanding of how the interfacial cation is sustained hinders efforts to address this challenge. Here, we reveal that sustained AMC-enabled CO2 reduction in MEA systems relies on a dynamic interfacial cation replenishment mechanism, in which continuous cation transport from the anolyte to the cathode compensates for the rapid depletion of interfacial cations, a process particularly pronounced in CEM–MEA systems. Guided by these insights, we demonstrate that (CH3)4N+ can serve as an effective alternative to AMCs, achieving CO2RR performance comparable to that of Cs+ in MEA systems. Crucially, the high solubility and strong hygroscopicity of (CH3)4NHCO3, together with the reduced crossover of (CH3)4N+, effectively suppress salt precipitation. Integrating this precipitation-free cation system with a continuous cation recovery unit enabled long-term CO2 electrolysis: an AEM–MEA operated continuously for over 4200 h without disassembly at 100 mA cm−2, with the CO Faradaic efficiency (FECO) maintained above 90%, and a CEM–MEA operated intermittently for a cumulative 380 h at 50 mA cm−2 with FECO above 80%. These results open a promising route toward durable, precipitation-free CO2 electrolysis.

item.title: Phase‐Change‐Induced Dual Electric Fields Over Atomically Bonded MicCu2O@Cu‐TCPP Heterojunctions for Synergistic Photocatalysis
item.description:
A phase-change microcapsule/p–n heterojunction system generates synergistic thermal and photoelectric fields under light irradiation. The local temperature gradient induced by the phase-change material creates a thermoelectric field via the Seebeck effect, which cooperates with the built-in electric field to promote charge separation. Consequently, MicCu2O@Cu-TCPP exhibits highly efficient and selective benzylamine oxidation.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic technology is essential for sustainable chemical synthesis but is constrained by charge recombination and thermal accumulation, which reduce quantum efficiency. Although heterojunctions enhance charge separation, conventional systems fail to alleviate thermally enhanced recombination.
